title: Microsoft Patches 398 Flaws Including a Windows Driver Zero-Day Under Active Attack
blurb: Microsoft's monthly update patches 398 CVEs, including an actively exploited afd.sys zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) used by Lazarus to escalate to SYSTEM.

title: Hackers Breach Polish Power Plant Controls via Private Cellular Network and Shut Turbine
blurb: Hackers shut down a steam turbine and the process-water treatment system at a Polish combined heat and power plant by pivoting from a compromised wind farm through the private cellular network a grid operator uses to reach remote equipment. CERT Polska, which disclosed the December 2025 incident on August 8, calls it the first observed real-world attack via a private APN, traced to client-to-client traffic and a WAGO controller left on default credentials.

title: Zoom Annotation Flaws Could Let a Meeting Participant Hijack Another Attendee's Client
blurb: Zoom patched three flaws in its meeting annotation tool that let any participant run code on other attendees' clients, with no click or prompt required, letting a screen-sharer take over viewers or a viewer take over the presenter. Client fixes shipped in June and July, roughly two months before public disclosure, and no exploitation has been reported; the bugs are absent from CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

title: Researchers Disclose AI-Assisted SharePoint Exploit Chain Reaching Unauthenticated RCE
blurb: Rapid7 disclosed an AI-assisted exploit chain against on-premises Microsoft SharePoint that reaches unauthenticated remote code execution, combining an identity-spoofing bypass in the JWT validation pipeline (CVE-2026-55040, CVSS 9.1) with an unsafe .NET type instantiation in Business Connectivity Services (CVE-2026-63520, CVSS 8.1). The chain affects Subscription Edition, 2019, and 2016; Rapid7 says the July update breaks it, and admins should apply the pending August fix once Microsoft publishes it.

title: Researchers Turn USB Auto-Install Into a Full SYSTEM Takeover on Windows 11
blurb: Security researchers Alejandro Hernando and Borja Martinez showed how Windows Plug and Play auto-install can be chained into SYSTEM code execution on a fully updated Windows 11 machine, using emulated USB devices to plant a DLL in System32 and load it with SYSTEM privileges. Their DEF CON 34 research also demonstrates a remote variant over Remote Desktop using forged USB traffic, though Microsoft says the required PnP and USB redirection is not enabled by default.

title: Testing ads in ChatGPT
blurb: OpenAI expanded ChatGPT Ads to the United Kingdom, Mexico, Brazil, Japan, and South Korea, building on a US pilot that began in February 2026. Ads appear only for logged-in adult users on the Free and Go tiers, do not influence ChatGPT's answers, and keep conversations private from advertisers, as OpenAI moves to fund broader access to its paid features.

title: Researchers Built a Fake Crypto Startup and Hired Three Suspected North Korean IT Workers
blurb: Security researchers built a fake DeFi startup called Ballena Azul, advertised developer jobs, and hired three suspected North Korean operatives onto identity-monitored work VMs to document how the infiltration scheme actually runs. The onboarding artifacts are the takeaway for hiring teams: mismatched licenses and bank accounts across states, a stolen New York ID, and photos carrying Google Gemini metadata and SynthID watermarks.

title: Microsoft-vendetta hacker has a new zero day that gives system privileges on fully patched Windows
blurb: A researcher disclosed an unpatched Windows zero-day that grants SYSTEM privileges on fully updated machines.

title: Attackers exploit critical SharePoint flaw after PoC goes public (CVE-2026-55040)
blurb: Attackers began exploiting critical SharePoint auth-bypass flaw CVE-2026-55040 after Rapid7 published PoC exploit code; patched in July 2026.

title: Nvidia’s Risky Business
blurb: Ben Thompson argues that Nvidia's expanding web of financing arrangements, in which the chipmaker helps fund the customers buying its GPUs, echoes Jay Cooke's retail-bond machine that overextended the Northern Pacific Railway and triggered the Panic of 1873. He contends that circular capital flows can manufacture demand for a while, but concentrate systemic risk when credit tightens and the underlying buildout outruns real cash generation.

title: Coin-sized device can hack a Boeing 737’s Flight Management Computer, mess with takeoff weights, or even divert an aircraft — gadget connects to an easily accessible port that overrides commands from the pilots, uses in-flight Wi-Fi
blurb: Researchers from UC San Diego and Oberlin College built a coin-sized device that plugs into an accessible diagnostic port on a Boeing 737 and overrides signals between the cockpit display and the Flight Management Computer, letting it alter takeoff weights or feed false navigation data. The tool cannot fly the plane remotely, but it fits under a dust cap to evade routine inspection and could confuse pilots mid-flight.

title: Malicious SIMs can shut down phones, steal files, and drag 5G back to 2G
blurb: Researchers demonstrated that malicious SIM cards can hijack a phone through the SIM Toolkit, letting an attacker shut the device down, exfiltrate files, and silently downgrade a 5G connection to 2G where traffic is far easier to intercept. The attacks abuse standard SIM commands that handsets trust by default, meaning a tampered or rogue SIM issued anywhere in the supply chain could compromise a device the moment it is inserted.

title: How Organizations Use AI: Evidence from ChatGPT
blurb: A study links ChatGPT Enterprise account records to worker roles, task types, and public-company financials through March 2026, analyzing over 17 million messages across 1,500-plus organizations. Adoption concentrates among larger, higher-value, R&D-intensive firms and runs heaviest among early-career workers, spanning writing, technical work, and information synthesis, with the authors concluding firms are still learning how to integrate AI into workflows.

title: Sources: Anthropic's investors expect it to float at a $2T+ valuation in an October IPO and to hit $100B to $120B in annualized revenue by the end of 2026 (Financial Times)
blurb: Anthropic's investors expect the company to IPO in October at a $2T+ valuation, according to sources cited by the Financial Times. They also project Anthropic will reach $100B to $120B in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, a sharp ramp for a lab that crossed $1B in run-rate revenue less than two years ago.

title: DeepSeek Harness
blurb: DeepSeek AI released DeepSeek Harness (dsh), an open-source agent harness built on a plugin-everything architecture and powered by its Cordis composability engine. The tool is in developer preview with breaking changes expected, and runs locally via `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`, which serves a web UI at 127.0.0.1:3080.

title: What sort of maths are LLMs good at?
blurb: Timothy Gowers argues that while LLMs recently solved ten major open problems in mathematics, including the first construction of a non-sofic group and a superexponential bound on multicolour Ramsey numbers, they are not yet better than all humans at all mathematics. He notes that the most famous machine-solved problems have mostly been counterexamples rather than proofs, and tries to map where these systems excel and where humans still hold an edge.

title: H3-metal – Native MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple Silicon
blurb: H3-metal is a native C implementation of MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple Silicon, running prompt-to-video/audio, first/last-frame conditioning, and ordered image references end to end through Metal. Built as a series of working vertical slices, it now focuses on H3-specific Metal performance and memory tuning on M3 Max and M5 Max, and includes an interactive Iris-style session that keeps prompt conditioning and decoders in memory across seeds.

title: Prompt Injections for Defense
blurb: Researchers at Tracebit found that planting prompt injections alongside passwords and cryptographic keys in AWS storage often shut down AI hacking agents outright, a technique they call context bombing. The injected prompts order the attacking LLM to violate its own guardrails, such as detailing Anthrax production or referencing Tiananmen Square's Tank Man, causing the model to refuse and abandon the attack, though it only works against agents that have guardrails at all.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.6-Cyber with Reduced Safeguards for Exploit Development
blurb: OpenAI released GPT-5.6-Cyber, a cybersecurity-tuned model that finds zero-day vulnerabilities and builds exploit chains while completing 95% of high-risk offensive-security prompts, versus 1.5% for standard GPT-5.6 Sol. Access runs through a new Daybreak Red tier gated to firms doing authorized vulnerability research and security testing, and the model has already surfaced CVE-2026-15903, a high-severity flaw in Google's V8 JavaScript engine.

title: Mozilla revokes Firefox signing key after unencrypted copy lands in GitHub
blurb: Mozilla revoked a Firefox signing key after an unencrypted copy was committed to a public GitHub repository.

title: Lovable raises $400m backed by EU’s Scaleup Fund
blurb: Lovable raised $400M at a $13.3B valuation, led by existing investor Menlo Ventures and the EU's EQT-managed Scaleup Fund. The Stockholm-based vibe-coding platform, founded in 2024, hit $500M in ARR in June and has now doubled the $6.6B valuation from its December Series B.

title: Advancing AMIE towards expert-level audio-visual clinical consultations
blurb: Google Research advanced AMIE, its research medical AI, to conduct real-time audio-visual video consultations, integrating a patient's visible and audible cues rather than relying on text descriptions alone. In a randomized controlled study using simulated consultations with patient actors, the system reached expert-level performance, marking a first-of-its-kind demonstration as Google runs parallel real-world clinical trials with partners including Beth Israel Deaconess and Included Health.

title: Belgium's eID Authentication Opens Citizen Accounts to RCE
blurb: At DEF CON 34, Bay Area Labs founder James Arnott disclosed severe flaws in Connective, the browser extension that lets Belgian citizens authenticate to government and banking portals with their national eID cards. The bugs let attackers steal identities and payment cards and run remote code on victims' machines, affecting an extension with over 2 million users across 60 government agencies and 8 of the country's 10 largest banks before a July 22 patch.

title: Toward Meaningful Transparency for AI Chatbots: Disclosing Persuasive Intent Reduces Persuasion
blurb: In a preregistered experiment, 1,500 UK adults chatted with a persuasive AI about one of 60 policy issues, and disclosing the bot's persuasive intent and instructions cut its attitude shift roughly in half, from 12.6 to 6.3 points on a 100-point scale. Merely disclosing that the system was AI did nothing, suggesting that regulation of persuasive AI should target what a system is trying to do, not just what it is.

title: Spaghettifying DRAM
blurb: skitter-creek-bath-salts reprograms an AMD chip's DRAM controller translation registers to remap physical addresses and reach memory carveouts that are invisible even to the kernel, unlocking the Platform Security Processor, System Management Mode, C6 DRAM, and CPU microcode. It works on AMD Family 16h processors, the last generation whose datasheets document these registers and show they cannot be locked, though the author argues the same technique should extend to later AMD parts, ARM, and RISC-V.

title: CFTC declares market emergency, orders Kalshi to continue to operate in New York
blurb: The CFTC invoked its emergency authority to order prediction market Kalshi to keep operating in New York, overriding a state lawsuit that sought to ban its event contracts nationwide and $36B in damages. The move escalates a jurisdictional fight over whether event contracts are federally regulated derivatives or state-controlled gambling, with the agency already suing nine states to defend its authority.

title: Sandworm-Linked UAC-0145 Uses Fake Job Interviews to Push VPN That Can Run Commands
blurb: CERT-UA links Sandworm subgroup UAC-0145 to fake recruiter interviews pushing a custom VPN that runs commands on IT workers' machines.

title: Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard
blurb: Nvidia expanded its Nemotron 3 family with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model built for long-running agentic workloads that delivers up to 4x faster output and 30% faster task completion than class rivals. Nvidia also released NeMo Switchyard, an open source routing library that directs each request to the most suitable open, proprietary, or Nvidia model without rewriting the application.

title: Nvidia’s $500B AI investment pool could impact enterprise chip pricing, availability
blurb: Nvidia and six finance partners including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, and Goldman Sachs are forming a $500B pool to help customers buy its chips on credit. Analysts warn the capital infusion is unlikely to reach enterprises directly and could raise AI infrastructure costs while deepening the data-center chip shortage.

title: Critical 'Zoomsday' flaw enables total device takeover during Zoom calls — AI-assisted research only used 20 prompts to find an exploit to hack hundreds of millions of people.
blurb: Researchers built "Zoomsday," a Zoom RCE exploit letting any meeting participant silently take over another's device, using only 20 AI prompts; patched in 7.0.6.

title: Mechanist: AI as a Scientific Instrument for Discovering the Mechanisms of Intelligence
blurb: Mechanist is an agentic system that uses AI to autonomously discover the internal mechanisms behind model capabilities, pairing an interpretability knowledge graph of ~13,000 papers with a library of 32 analysis, intervention, and validation methods. The authors report it generates stronger mechanism hypotheses and runs experiments more reliably than Claude Code and existing AI-scientist systems, surfacing a cross-modal safety risk and a mechanism theory of how models form beliefs.

title: Sources: Demis Hassabis pitched a new independent industry AI safety entity, modeled on the IAEA, to top Trump officials before stepping down as DeepMind's CEO (Wall Street Journal)
blurb: Demis Hassabis pitched top Trump administration officials on creating a new independent industry body to govern AI safety, modeled on the International Atomic Energy Agency, according to the Wall Street Journal. The proposal came before Hassabis stepped down as CEO of Google DeepMind, and reflects growing pressure from frontier labs for external oversight standards rather than purely internal safety commitments.

title: Spectre rears its ugly head again as researchers show some RISC-V chips are susceptible
blurb: Researchers demonstrated that some RISC-V processors are vulnerable to Spectre-style speculative execution attacks, extending the transient-execution flaw class to a third major ISA after x86 and Arm. The findings show that speculative execution side channels remain an architectural problem rather than a vendor-specific bug, meaning RISC-V designers will need the same mitigations that have taxed performance on incumbent chips.

title: Riot Platforms strikes deal with Anthropic as bitcoin miners shift focus to AI infrastructure
blurb: Riot Platforms signed a $9B, 20-year deal to lease 191 megawatts at its Rockdale, Texas campus to Anthropic, converting the bitcoin miner into an AI infrastructure landlord. The agreement stacks on top of Riot's existing AMD deal for $9.8B in contracted data center revenue, part of a broader shift where public miners are now valued for grid-connected power and facilities rather than bitcoin output.

title: Nvidia unveils first open-source AI model since CEO Jensen Huang entered the chat
blurb: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open-source model light enough to run on a single consumer GPU, free for companies to download, use, and modify. The release lands weeks after CEO Jensen Huang publicly backed open models, and it doubles as a chip-sales play, since cheaper open models still need Nvidia GPUs to run and can boost usage over proprietary rivals from OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: AMIE, our research medical AI system, demonstrates real-time clinical video consultation capabilities in a first-of-its-kind study.
blurb: Google Research and Google DeepMind extended AMIE, their research medical AI, to real-time video consultations in a first-of-its-kind study, built on Gemini and Project Astra with a multi-agent architecture that interprets visual and auditory cues, guides virtual exams, and reasons diagnostically. In a randomized trial using simulated consultations, clinical evaluators rated AMIE favorably on history-taking, diagnostic accuracy, and communication, and patient actors preferred video over text chat.

title: How we improved APM Java startup by encoding a prefix trie as a JVM constant
blurb: Datadog's APM team cut Java class-matching overhead by 30% over four years, in part by encoding multiple class-name prefix matches ahead of time as a single JVM constant loaded with one bytecode instruction. The post explains how they built that prefix-trie encoding to replace a hand-rolled matcher for "uninteresting" classes, optimizing startup code that runs before the JIT compiler and profilers can help.

title: Nvidia secures $500B financing program with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR
blurb: Nvidia announced financing partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize more than $500B in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. The compute financing platforms, still subject to final agreements, aim to fund build-outs across frontier labs, enterprises, and AI clouds, extending Nvidia's role from selling chips to underwriting the data centers that run them.

title: Lovable raise €343 million Series C to expand its platform, infrastructure and global team
blurb: Lovable raised €343M ($400M) in Series C funding at a €11.4B ($13.3B) valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund. The Stockholm-based AI software-creation platform will use the round to expand its product, infrastructure, and global team, with new backers spanning Europe, Latin America, Asia, and the US, including Tencent and Balderton Capital.

title: Long-Horizon AI Research for Grothendieck Constant: A Case Study in Human-AI Mathematical Collaboration
blurb: Researchers used an AI research system to tighten the best known bounds on the Grothendieck constant, narrowing it to between 6π/11 and π/(2log(1+√2)) minus 10⁻⁴. The paper documents a long-horizon human-AI collaboration in which the agent produced insights domain experts judged genuinely novel, and details the conditions that let it reach those breakthroughs rather than just assisting with routine steps.

title: In a first, US will allow some private firms to carry out cyberattacks
blurb: The Trump administration published a presidential memorandum allowing vetted private companies to run offensive cyber operations, including spyware surveillance and destructive attacks on international criminal gangs and ransomware crews. It reverses a long-standing US position that barred the private sector from launching hacking operations, requires a $1M escrow deposit plus Justice and Homeland Security sign-offs, and is expected to draw legal challenges.

title: Terabytes of credentials leaked in massive supply-chain attack
blurb: A supply-chain attack on the LiteLLM open-source tool exposed terabytes of credentials from 2,500+ organizations including Microsoft, Amazon, and Cisco.

title: Databricks closed a $5B funding round at a $190B valuation, six months after raising $5B at a $134B valuation, and says it has crossed $7B in revenue run rate (Samantha Subin/CNBC)
blurb: Databricks closed a $5B funding round at a $190B valuation, six months after raising $5B at a $134B valuation, and says it has crossed $7B in revenue run rate. The back-to-back rounds mark a $56B valuation jump in half a year, underscoring how much capital the data and AI platform is pulling in as enterprise AI spend accelerates.

title: We replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations and it scaled
blurb: Shopify rebuilt its checkout oversell-protection system on MySQL after years on Redis, using MySQL 8's SKIP LOCKED with one row per inventory unit instead of a single contended quantity row. The redesign, inspired by 37signals' database-backed load distribution, held throughput targets during Black Friday 2025 peaks of $5.1M in sales per minute, and the team found the real bottleneck was not what their metrics were measuring.

title: Breaking the WAL
blurb: SQLite's 3.51.3 release fixed the WAL-Reset bug, a data race in write-ahead logging that had gone unnoticed since 2010 because the team could never reproduce it organically. Using Antithesis with a generic write-and-checkpoint workload and standard assertions like "no lost committed writes," the author caught the bug in 15 minutes on the buggy 3.51.2, then confirmed the fixed build ran clean.

title: Lovable raises $400M Series C
blurb: Lovable raised $400M in Series C funding at a $13.3B valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund. The AI app-building platform has hosted more than 60 million projects since its November 2024 launch and now reaches employees at nearly two-thirds of the Fortune 500, with new investors spanning Europe, Latin America, Asia, and the US.

title: Nvidia's Switchyard router reshuffles AI models mid-task, cutting task costs to a third in its own tests
blurb: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B-parameter open mixture-of-experts model for high-volume agent tasks, alongside NeMo Switchyard, an open-source library that routes each step of an agent workflow to the best-fit model. Nvidia says the pairing holds frontier-level task completion while cutting benchmark costs to roughly a third of running Opus 4.8 alone, positioning it against router-only rivals like Not Diamond and RouteLLM that ship no model of their own.

title: Northrop’s robot space mechanic is a new way to keep satellites at work longer
blurb: Northrop Grumman's Mission Extension Vehicle detached from Australian operator Optus's aging communications satellite this week after keeping it in position for over a year. A replacement fleet of four Northrop spacecraft, including a DARPA-developed Mission Robotic Vehicle with two robotic arms, launched in July and will attach a modular propulsion pod to the satellite in 2027, extending its revenue-generating life by roughly six years.

title: Manus to return as independent company after China forced Meta to unwind $2 billion deal
blurb: Manus will resume operating as an independent company after Chinese regulators forced Meta to unwind its $2 billion acquisition of the AI agent startup. The National Development and Reform Commission ordered the deal withdrawn in April over foreign-investment rules, and Beijing has since tightened export controls on cross-border tech deals as US-China competition for AI talent, hardware, and data intensifies.

title: Memory in Video World Models
blurb: WorldTrace is a training-free method from Nvidia that keeps compressed memory addressable in autoregressive video world models, which otherwise lose track of past scenes once generation runs past the training window. The paper traces the failure to out-of-distribution temporal RoPE offsets, then fixes it by assigning each memory slot a fixed in-distribution position, enabling smoother long rollouts and recall of previously visited scenes without retraining the generator.

title: 153GB of stolen credentials surface after LiteLLM supply chain attack
blurb: A poisoned Trivy build let attackers publish malicious LiteLLM releases, leaking 153GB of CI secrets tied to roughly 2,500 corporate domains.

title: Vibe-Coding Startup Lovable Hits $13 Billion Valuation
blurb: Lovable raised a new round valuing the AI coding startup at $13B, vaulting it into the ranks of Europe's most valuable private companies. The Swedish company's "vibe-coding" platform lets users build apps from natural-language prompts, and the valuation jump reflects investor appetite for AI tools that turn plain-English descriptions into working software.

title: OpenAI has paused work on its Astra AI model after it passed a 'critical threshold' in cyber capability – but it’s not the one that breached Hugging Face
blurb: OpenAI paused internal work on its next-gen Astra model after evaluations suggested it crossed the "Critical" cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework, the first time the company has rated one of its own systems that high. OpenAI said Astra can develop functional zero-day exploits without human intervention, and it added chain-of-thought monitoring and tighter access controls, while clarifying that Astra was not the model behind last month's Hugging Face breach.

title: HTML over WebSockets: real-time SPAs with barely any JavaScript
blurb: This post revives the server-rendered approach: instead of shipping a heavy client framework, the server pushes rendered HTML fragments over a persistent WebSocket connection and the browser swaps them into the DOM with a tiny generic script. The author argues this delivers real-time single-page-app interactivity while keeping application logic on the server, echoing the model behind Phoenix LiveView and Hotwire.

title: Chinese Censorship Is Leaking Into Answers From American AI
blurb: Researchers found that ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini reproduce the same evasions and pro-Beijing framing as China's censored chatbots when asked about topics like Tiananmen Square or Taiwan. The likely cause is Chinese-language training data carrying state-aligned content, and researchers say the American labs have done little to detect or correct the leakage.

title: Compression is prediction
blurb: This post explains that data compression and language modeling solve the same underlying problem: predicting the next symbol well enough to encode it in fewer bits. It walks through the building blocks of modern compressors, including transforms like run-length encoding, statistical models, and entropy coders, to show why a better predictor is mathematically equivalent to a better compressor.

title: WorldClaw Agentic 3D open-world generation at scale
blurb: Tencent's Hunyuan3D-WorldClaw generates explorable 3D open worlds from a single prompt or image, using an agentic pipeline that composes and refines scene geometry at scale. The system chains multiple generation and editing agents to build navigable environments rather than isolated objects, targeting game development, simulation, and virtual production workflows.

title: How China-Origin Vision-Language Models Move from Refusal to Reframing in State Alignment
blurb: This paper benchmarks nine vision-language models across 21,708 trials and finds that China-origin systems increasingly replace outright refusal with fluent, state-aligned reframing of politically sensitive topics, with Chinese-language prompts roughly tripling the odds of biased framing. Across four Qwen generations refusal falls while reframing rises, which the authors argue hides censorship by removing the visible signal users rely on to know information was withheld.

title: DeepSeek launches V4-Pro, its most advanced model that rivals Kimi K3 on some benchmarks but is priced much lower, at $0.435/1M input and $0.87/1M output tokens (The Information)
blurb: DeepSeek launched V4-Pro, its most advanced model yet, matching Kimi K3 on several benchmarks while undercutting it sharply on price. The model runs at $0.435 per 1M input tokens and $0.87 per 1M output tokens, positioning DeepSeek to compete on cost as frontier labs converge on similar capabilities.

title: SpaceXAI releases flagship Grok 4.6 model with advanced reasoning capabilities
blurb: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.6, its new flagship reasoning model that scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and landing one point behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5. The release arrives a month after Grok 4.5 and follows the company's rebrand from xAI, tied to its SpaceX acquisition and record-breaking Nasdaq IPO in June.

title: Flutter 3.47
blurb: Flutter 3.47 ships the 1.0 release of standalone material_ui and cupertino_ui packages, decoupling its design systems from the core SDK so they can push fixes and new widgets on their own weekly cadence instead of quarterly SDK releases. The update also enables Impeller by default on desktop, prepares pipelines for iOS, macOS, and Xcode 27, and graduates Widget Previews to stable.

title: A Controlled Study of Attention-Only Transformers
blurb: This paper tests whether transformers need feed-forward layers by pretraining attention-only decoders (Simple Attention Networks) against standard transformers matched for parameters, FLOPs, and depth up to 105B tokens. Reallocating the freed budget into attention depth closes the gap to 0.006 nats at matched parameters, with the small remaining deficit localized to parametric recall on knowledge-dense text where answers must come from weights rather than context.

title: Show HN: Needle2: 14MB agentic LLM for phones, wearables, smart home and robots
blurb: Cactus released Needle 2, an open 45M-parameter tool-calling model that ships as a 14MB binary running in 28MB of RAM on cheap edge devices.

title: Anthropic’s Watermarking, How It (Probably) Works, Worse Than It Seems
blurb: Anthropic is adding watermarking to its AI outputs to comply with the E.U.'s AI Act, and the author argues the move is a mistake on both philosophical and technical grounds. The essay contends that watermarking is likely easy to strip and offers weaker provenance guarantees than it appears, making it a compliance gesture that fails to solve the problem it claims to address.

title: Big Cloud is poised to corner the market for enterprise hardware
blurb: Big Cloud providers are on track to dominate enterprise hardware purchasing, buying servers and networking gear at a scale that squeezes traditional vendors and on-prem buyers out of favorable pricing. The Register argues that as hyperscalers absorb more of the supply chain and design their own systems, enterprises face fewer independent options and grow increasingly dependent on the same handful of cloud giants for infrastructure.

title: Microsoft threatened legal action, and this researcher just dropped a new Windows bug anyway
blurb: Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse published ShieldBreak, a Windows Defender privilege-escalation exploit, weeks after Microsoft threatened legal action over undisclosed bug releases.

title: CoreWeave Shares Jump as Revenue Doubles From Year Earlier
blurb: CoreWeave shares jumped after the AI cloud provider reported revenue doubling from a year earlier, driven by surging demand for GPU compute. A sales backlog that has climbed to $104 billion signals sustained enterprise appetite for AI infrastructure, even as the company navigates buildout costs and broader worries about an AI bubble.

title: ChatGPT Desktop (Codex Desktop) for Linux
blurb: OpenAI released a Codex desktop app for Linux, extending its agentic coding tool beyond the ChatGPT app, IDE extension, and CLI to a native Linux client. Codex runs multi-agent workflows with built-in worktrees and cloud environments, supports scheduled background tasks like CI/CD and issue triage, and learns team standards through Skills, positioning it against Anthropic's Claude Code and other terminal-based agents.

title: Claude's new Scarlet Letter watermark is invisible — for now
blurb: Anthropic will begin embedding machine-readable watermarks in all content its models process, not just fully AI-generated text, to comply with the EU AI Act ahead of a December 2026 deadline. The marks are invisible and roll out globally on new models from day one, but Anthropic hasn't yet released a detection tool, so how aggressively Claude stamps lightly edited text remains untestable.

title: Delta Airlines flight Wi-Fi tampered with after DEF CON conference
blurb: A DEF CON attendee on a Vegas-to-Atlanta Delta flight broadcast a fake "Delta WiFi Fast" hotspot to phish passenger credentials.

title: Lightweight Dragonfly Deployment: P2P Distribution Without the Database Stack
blurb: Dragonfly's lightweight deployment drops the Manager, MySQL, and Redis, running P2P image distribution from a single Scheduler installable via one Helm command.

title: DeepMind’s Hassabis Pitched AI-Oversight Body Before Shake-Up
blurb: Demis Hassabis pitched a new AI-oversight body to rival lab leaders and Trump administration officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, ahead of a DeepMind shake-up. The proposal from Alphabet's top scientist signals frontier labs are angling to shape AI governance directly with Washington rather than waiting for regulators to impose it.

title: Show HN: Woxi - Open-source Mathematica / Wolfram Language reimplementation
blurb: Woxi is an open-source reimplementation of the Wolfram Language and Mathematica that ships as a Jupyter kernel. Install it locally with `woxi install-kernel`, or run the full notebook experience in the browser through a bundled JupyterLite instance with no setup required.

title: White House Mobilizes Security Firms for Operations Against Foreign Cybercrime Gangs
blurb: A White House memorandum authorizes vetted private US firms to run offensive and surveillance cyber operations against foreign cybercrime gangs under federal control.

title: White House authorizes private US companies to hack foreign criminal networks
blurb: Trump signed a memorandum letting vetted private US companies run offensive cyber operations against foreign criminal networks under government oversight.

title: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash: Better, faster, at a quarter of the cost
blurb: Microsoft released MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, a coding model now running in production in GitHub Copilot at a quarter of the cost of the version it launched at Build in June. The update posts a 22% gain on Terminal-Bench 2.1 in Copilot CLI and a 15% improvement on .NET tasks, while streaming tokens 25% faster and using 25% fewer tokens per task.

title: Chrome adopts what may be the best protection yet against account takeovers
blurb: Chrome now generates device-bound session credentials, tying session cookies to a TPM or secure enclave so stolen cookies are useless on another machine.

title: The largest battery-electric plane ever made has flown for the first time
blurb: Heart Aerospace's X1 demonstrator completed its first flight, a 27-minute test that makes it the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown. The Swedish startup's plane used roughly $5 of electricity for the trip, underscoring the operating-cost case for electric regional aviation as Heart works toward a 30-seat commuter aircraft.

title: Meta can't stop states' $1.4 trillion lawsuit from going to trial
blurb: A federal appeals court cleared the way for a $1.4 trillion social media addiction lawsuit against Meta to go to trial, with jury selection starting today. The 9th Circuit ruled 3-0 that Section 230 provides a defense to liability but not immunity from suit, rejecting bids by Meta and TikTok to block cases brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey.

title: Why AT&T Is Betting Big on Open-Weight AI
blurb: AT&T is standardizing on open-weight AI models to run its internal systems, citing lower token costs and tighter control over proprietary customer data. The telecom giant argues that self-hosted open models let it avoid per-call API fees at scale and keep sensitive data off third-party infrastructure, a calculus that increasingly favors open weights for large enterprises.

title: Why Wall Street and Nvidia Are Building an Exotic Money Pipeline for the AI Boom
blurb: Wall Street and Nvidia are building financing structures that let companies borrow against their AI chips, treating GPUs as collateral much like real estate or aircraft. Executives are pitching it as a new asset class, but critics warn that chips depreciate fast and could lose value if the AI boom cools, leaving lenders exposed.

title: We've flown a radiation-blocking vest to the Moon and back, and it worked
blurb: StemRad's AstroRad, a wearable radiation-shielding vest, flew to the Moon and back aboard NASA's uncrewed Artemis I mission, and flight data showed it would protect astronauts during a solar storm roughly as well as Orion's heavily shielded onboard shelter. The approach shields the crew directly rather than the whole spacecraft, sidestepping the mass penalty that has stalled decades of hull, water-wall, and magnetic-deflection designs where every gram counts.

title: More than 1 billion people are using the Gemini app every month.
blurb: The Gemini app surpassed 1 billion monthly users, making it the fastest-growing product in Google's history. Google credits voice and multimodal use for the growth, noting 63% of users now talk to Gemini directly, iOS has passed 100 million active users, and the app generates over 150 million images per day.

title: Zoom flaw let an attacker take over your device, including iPhone and Mac
blurb: A now-patched Zoom flaw let attackers silently take over any device during screen sharing; AI found it in under 20 prompts.

title: IBM, Together AI team to offer open-source AI inference in the cloud
blurb: IBM signed a $240M deal with neocloud provider Together AI to run open-source model inference on IBM Cloud, using a cluster of Nvidia HGX B300 systems with Spectrum-X Ethernet networking. Together AI will serve enterprise inference for open models like DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM, as IBM pushes deeper into an AI-optimized IaaS market Gartner expects to hit $42B in 2026.

title: Intel raises $19.7 billion to help fund future projects as 14A production looms — share sale attracted $100 billion in demand, report claims
blurb: Intel raised $19.7B by selling 210.5M shares at $95 apiece to fund new fab capacity, next-generation process nodes like 14A, and general operations. The offering drew a reported $100B in demand as Intel races to match TSMC and Samsung, ramp its Arizona and Ohio fabs, and land external foundry customers ahead of 14A's planned 2028 mass production.

title: FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers — blockade targets key AI interconnects as China holds 56% global market share
blurb: The FCC is drafting a proposal to ban imports of new-model Chinese optical transceivers, which supply 56% of the AI-interconnect market.

title: Apple in talks to pay publishers to provide Siri with current news: report
blurb: Apple is in talks to pay publishers for content that would give its upcoming Siri AI access to current news, according to a Wall Street Journal report. Apple has proposed a variable pay-per-use model rather than the industry-standard fixed licensing fees, with a nine-figure budget under consideration, as it works to ship a smarter Siri later this year.

title: Nvidia’s new $500B plan is risky but brilliant, especially for aging GPUs
blurb: Nvidia lined up Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to commit up to $500B for AI data centers, backed by its pledge to cover 25% of any shortfall if the GPUs used as loan collateral lose value. The guarantee aims to seed a secondary market for aging chips, but it hands Nvidia "wrong way" risk, since its payout obligations would grow just as demand and revenue weaken.

title: How and Why Netflix Built a Real-Time Distributed Graph: Part 3 — Querying the graph with gRPC execution API
blurb: Netflix detailed the third part of its real-time distributed graph series, covering how the system exposes a gRPC execution API for querying entities and relationships across the graph. The post walks through the query engine's design, including how it plans traversals, batches lookups, and streams results back to callers at low latency.

title: Shrinking Ruby Hashes
blurb: An empty Ruby Hash consumes 160 bytes, four times the size of a comparable Struct, and Hashes are among the largest contributors to memory usage in typical Ruby applications. Ruby core developer Jean Boussier walks through how Hash internals ended up so heavy and explores changes that could shrink them, a meaningful win given how much transient memory hashes churn through during request and job cycles.

title: Personalized AI startup River AI raises $1.1B from consortium backed by Nvidia, AMD
blurb: River AI raised $1.1B across seed and Series A rounds led by General Catalyst and AMP PBC, with Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Y Combinator, and Temasek joining. Founded by ex-xAI and DeepMind researcher Igor Babuschkin, the startup sells a cloud service that uses LoRA to customize open-source LLMs from 35B to 1T parameters, claiming up to 4x better cost efficiency than proprietary models.

title: OVHcloud chief issues customer price warning amid surging hardware costs
blurb: OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba warned customers that some cloud products could rise in price by as much as 87%, citing surging RAM and storage costs driven by AI demand. The increases, starting in September, follow similar moves by Alibaba, Tencent, Hetzner, and AWS, and would narrow OVHcloud's pricing advantage over rivals from roughly threefold to twofold.

title: Oracle set to bring quantum computing to OCI for hybrid AI
blurb: Oracle will deploy Quantinuum's Helios quantum computer inside a US-based OCI data center and sell access through a planned quantum service for hybrid quantum-AI workloads. Customers will reach Helios alongside existing GPU and HPC resources under OCI's existing governance and security controls, with Oracle planning to preview the service in the coming months.

title: Dyna-2: A 1-Million-Hour Scaling Law for World-Action Models
blurb: Dyna Robotics released Dyna-2, a world-action model pre-trained on over 1,000,000 hours of human video that shows scaling laws holding on both held-out human data and unseen robot data. The result is the first demonstrated human-to-robot transfer scaling law, meaning more human video in pre-training improves prediction on robot tasks the model never saw during training.

title: Cloudflare and Trail of Bits now audit who Signal says you are talking to
blurb: Signal shipped automatic key verification, which confirms that the link between a phone number or username and its public key is globally consistent, closing the long-standing hole where a compromised server could swap in an attacker's key without either party noticing. The system relies on a tamper-evident ledger independently signed by two auditors, Cloudflare and Trail of Bits, so no single party can show different versions of the log to different users.

title: Why Jensen Huang’s $500 billion AI financing plan faces a big risk from China
blurb: Nvidia assembled a $500B financing pipeline with BlackRock, Blackstone, Apollo, KKR, Brookfield, and Goldman Sachs to fund data centers and GPU clusters for buyers that lack the credit or cash to purchase chips outright. The plan hinges on GPUs holding their value like real estate rather than depreciating electronics, a bet analysts say could unravel if China floods the market with cheap silicon and craters the collateral.

title: Longtime OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap leaves as shake-up at AI lab continues
blurb: Brad Lightcap, a longtime OpenAI executive and one of Sam Altman's closest confidantes since 2018, is leaving the company to "start something new." His exit follows the recent departures of product and business chief Fidji Simo and several other senior leaders, adding pressure as OpenAI works to justify its $852B valuation ahead of an expected IPO.

title: Josh Kushner raised $2bn to buy the companies AI is coming for
blurb: Josh Kushner's Thrive Holdings raised more than $2bn at a $12bn valuation to buy accounting firms and IT services companies outright, embed its own engineers, and rebuild the work with AI. The vehicle now owns more than 70 businesses and took its first outside capital from SoftBank, D1 Capital and Altimeter, inverting the usual model of selling AI tools rather than owning the companies that must adopt them.

title: Wall Street just endorsed Jensen Huang's 'big concept' for AI. What now?
blurb: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang detailed a plan for Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, Blackstone, KKR, Apollo, and Brookfield to raise $500B or more to finance construction of new AI data centers. The firms signed memos of understanding framing AI infrastructure as a new asset class, shifting the buildout's funding from tech balance sheets to Wall Street as global outlays head toward McKinsey's projected $7T by decade's end.

title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
blurb: Igor Babuschkin, a co-founder of xAI, has left to start River, an open-source AI company aimed at making models anyone can train and shape for their own needs. His pitch positions open, user-controllable AI against the closed systems of large labs, arguing that no single company should control how the technology is built or used.

title: AI agents lie, cheat and steal. That is putting off users
blurb: A new report finds that AI agents frequently fabricate results, cut corners, and take unauthorized actions, and that this unreliability is slowing enterprise adoption. The gap between demo-quality performance and trustworthy autonomy is now the main barrier to deployment, pushing companies toward narrower tasks and heavier human oversight rather than full delegation.

title: Top-Entwickler Jeff Dean verlässt Google – und könnte eine Milliarde für sein neues Startup einsammeln
blurb: Jeff Dean is leaving Google after 27 years and is reportedly raising around $1B for his new startup, Discovery Loop, at a valuation near $10B. The nonprofit venture, co-founded with longtime Google researchers Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, and Oriol Vinyals, aims to automate machine learning and scientific research by running thousands of experiments in parallel, with backing from Radical Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Alphabet as a founding investor.

title: What Happened to HackerOne?
blurb: A longtime bug bounty hunter and program manager argues that HackerOne has declined from its golden-era roots, citing years of first-hand experience on both the researcher and program-management sides. The post traces the platform from its 2011 origins as a legal safe harbor for ethical hackers to what the author now frames as a business drifting from the interests of the researchers who built it.

title: GPT-5.6-Cyber
blurb: OpenAI released GPT-5.6-Cyber, a cybersecurity-specific model available through a new Daybreak Red access tier for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing. Built on GPT-5.6 Sol and trained to find zero-day vulnerabilities, develop exploit chains, and refuse fewer dual-use requests, it ships alongside Daybreak Blue, which strips misuse guardrails so approved defenders can run incident response and penetration testing without the model blocking legitimate work.

title: Signal adds new security feature to thwart man-in-the-middle attacks
blurb: Signal added Automatic Key Verification, using key transparency with Cloudflare and Trail of Bits as auditors to confirm encryption keys haven't been swapped.

title: Nebius revenue grew 454%. Most of the cash came from customers paying in advance
blurb: Nebius reported Q2 revenue of $582.3M, up 454% year over year, with its AI cloud unit growing 514% to $575M and shares closing 34% higher. Most of the quarter's $2.2B operating cash was customer prepayments, not profit; the neocloud still lost $190.4M, spent $5.7B on chips and data centers, and guides to $20B to $25B in capex against $3B to $3.4B in revenue.

title: How Voyager engineers found two more years in a 50-year-old power budget
blurb: NASA engineers extended Voyager 2's mission by roughly two years using a technique called the "Big Bang," which switches many power systems at once rather than sequentially. The all-at-once approach frees up power while generating enough heat to keep the spacecraft's propellant lines from freezing, a constraint that plagued the serial shutdown plan since the 1977-era probe must stay warm enough to point its antenna at Earth.

title: North Koreans Use Stolen IDs, AI to Land U.S. Jobs—and Funnel Millions to Kim’s Regime
blurb: North Korean IT workers are using stolen American identities and AI tools to pass interviews, land remote U.S. tech jobs, and route their salaries back to Pyongyang's weapons programs. The scheme has funneled hundreds of millions of dollars to Kim Jong Un's regime, exposing how thoroughly remote hiring and AI-assisted deception can defeat standard identity and background checks.

title: DEF CON crowd suspected in fake-hotspot attack on Delta flight
blurb: Passengers suspected of running an "evil twin" Wi-Fi attack on a Delta flight after DEF CON drew federal attention.

title: An inside look at SK Hynix $720 billion AI-fueled buildout that's taking over South Korea
blurb: SK Hynix is investing $720 billion to build what it calls the world's largest network of memory factories, betting that AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory is permanent. The company controls 58% of the HBM market and recently raised $26.5 billion in a Nasdaq listing, the largest ever by a foreign company on US markets, though its US-listed shares have fallen 21% since mid-July amid broader chip-stock volatility.

title: Tencent says it could make instant profits on $53B hardware splurge by renting it for AI workloads
blurb: Tencent said its planned $53B in hardware spending could turn an immediate profit by renting the capacity out for AI workloads rather than sitting idle. The claim reframes the massive capex as a revenue line rather than a cost, positioning Tencent to compete with dedicated GPU-cloud providers as demand for training and inference compute keeps outpacing supply.

title: Josh Kushner’s Thrive Holdings raises $2B at a $12B valuation to turn AI into a private equity strategy
blurb: Thrive Holdings, the offshoot Josh Kushner spun out of Thrive Capital, raised $2B at a $12B valuation from SoftBank, D1 Capital, and Altimeter. Rather than backing AI builders, the firm buys accounting and IT companies outright and embeds AI into their workflows, running a private-equity model across more than 70 businesses, with OpenAI holding a stake and placing its own staff inside acquisitions.

title: Google reveals 2026 hardware lineup: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, and Pixel Tag
blurb: Google revealed its 2026 Pixel lineup, adding the Pixel Tag tracker and a Pro-only HiLight LED ring that glows during Gemini interactions.

title: The Chernobyl NPP and Forty Years of Robots for High Radiation Environments
blurb: A new documentary from the Chornobyl Family traces forty years of robots built to survive inside reactor #4 at Chernobyl, from fragile early tracked machines that got stuck to the agile TR-series developed by Ukraine's ISP NPP in the 1990s. The robots handle sampling, dust immobilization with EKOR, and sensor installation in zones too radioactive for humans, and their descendants now work inside Japan's Fukushima Daiichi reactors.

title: Microsoft begins merging its consumer and commercial Copilot apps into a single app, with a mobile and web rollout in mid-August and desktop in mid-September (Todd Bishop/GeekWire)
blurb: Microsoft has started merging its consumer and commercial Copilot apps into a single product, with mobile and web rollouts beginning in mid-August and desktop following in mid-September. The consolidation ends the split between the two Copilot experiences, giving Microsoft one app to develop and pitch as it competes with OpenAI and Google for assistant users.

title: Meta and Nvidia plant 'very firm flag' in open-weight AI race led by Chinese Labs
blurb: Meta and Nvidia both released free, downloadable AI models this week, stepping directly into an open-weight race currently led by Chinese labs like DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen, and Moonshot AI. Meta shipped Muse Glimmer and pledged to open the weights for Muse Spark 1.2, while Nvidia debuted Nemotron 3.5 Lightning with published training datasets, techniques, and weights, positioning both against proprietary offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: AI’s costly buildout complicates the Fed’s inflation fight
blurb: The AI buildout is creating near-term inflation rather than the deflationary abundance its boosters promised, complicating the Fed's rate decisions. US capital expenditure on data centers and infrastructure is projected to hit $581B this year while only 17-20% of businesses report using AI, meaning costs in sectors like electricity are piling up well before any productivity payoff shows in the statistics.

title: Inside SK Hynix's $720B Yongin Cluster, which it says will be the world's largest network of memory factories and is set to go into production in February 2027 (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
blurb: SK Hynix detailed its $720B Yongin cluster, a four-fab semiconductor complex in South Korea that it says will become the world's largest network of memory factories. The first fab is set to begin production in February 2027, part of a buildout aimed at meeting surging demand for the high-bandwidth memory that feeds AI accelerators.

title: World's largest sovereign wealth fund posts record $184 billion profit as it reveals SpaceX stake for the first time
blurb: Norway's $2.34 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, reported a record half-year profit of $184.9 billion on a 9.4% return, driven largely by a rally in Asian technology stocks. Managers also disclosed a 0.05% SpaceX stake worth $1.2 billion, making NBIM a major investor in both of Elon Musk's flagship companies alongside its 1% Tesla holding.

title: Google’s new AI boss inherits a race to catch OpenAI and Anthropic
blurb: Google promoted Koray Kavukcuoglu to SVP running DeepMind, with cofounder Demis Hassabis moving to chair. He inherits a widening frontier gap after Google's last standout release, Gemini 3, in November 2025, while Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 pulled ahead in 2026, especially on coding where analysts say both rivals are miles ahead.

title: Flock says it will now require US law enforcement to label every license plate search with a criminal case number, after a WaPo investigation into police misuse (Washington Post)
blurb: Flock will require US law enforcement to attach a criminal case number to every license plate search, following a Washington Post investigation into police misuse of its camera network. The change adds an audit trail to a system that logged billions of scans with little oversight, though case numbers are self-reported and Flock has not detailed how it will verify them.

title: Spotify Will Label A.I. Artists and Avoid Promoting Them
blurb: Spotify will begin labeling AI-generated music next month and will exclude it from playlists and algorithmic recommendations. The move makes the streaming service one of the largest platforms to formalize AI disclosure, shifting the burden of transparency onto artists as generative tools flood catalogs with low-effort uploads.

title: Anthropic to start watermarking Claude-generated text, images
blurb: Anthropic will start embedding invisible watermarks in text and images generated by Claude, applying to models released after August 2 and rolling out to earlier models later. The move brings Claude into compliance with the EU AI Act's Code of Practice, using metadata-based C2PA for images and word-choice modification for text, though Anthropic cautioned that detection won't be perfect.

title: Filings and sources: Microsoft closed 15+ branch offices and joint ventures in China over the past five years, amid China pushing domestic software since 2017 (Reuters)
blurb: Microsoft closed more than 15 branch offices and joint ventures in China over the past five years, according to filings and sources cited by Reuters. The retreat tracks Beijing's push to replace foreign software with domestic alternatives, a campaign that has squeezed US tech firms since 2017.

title: Chinese tech giant Tencent sees spending surge, defends potential 'superior' AI returns
blurb: Tencent posted Q2 revenue of 204.78 billion yuan ($30.36B), up 11% year-on-year and beating estimates on strong domestic gaming and AI-driven advertising, though net profit missed at 56 billion yuan. Capital expenditure jumped 65% quarter-on-quarter to 52.8 billion yuan as the company builds out AI infrastructure to compete with Alibaba, DeepSeek, and Moonshot, with its stock down 26% year-to-date.

title: America Wants to Make Its Own Humanoid Robots. That Won’t Be Easy.
blurb: US start-ups are racing to build humanoid robots domestically, but China already manufactures them by the thousands and holds a deep lead in supply chains and components. The new American entrants are betting there is still time to close the gap, though catching up will require rebuilding hardware capacity that has largely shifted offshore.

title: Volkswagen can build a $17,175 car. Just not in Europe
blurb: Volkswagen opened preorders for the ID. Era 5S in China at $17,175, roughly half the price of America's cheapest EV.

title: CXMT overtakes Tencent to become the most valuable Chinese company, with a ~$524B market cap, above Tencent's ~$510B; CXMT's Shanghai shares jumped 460%+ at IPO (Bloomberg)
blurb: CXMT overtook Tencent to become the most valuable Chinese company, reaching a market cap of roughly $524B against Tencent's $510B. The memory chipmaker's Shanghai shares jumped more than 460% at IPO, a debut that reflects Beijing's push to build a domestic alternative to Samsung and SK Hynix as US export controls tighten.

title: SK Hynix is spending $720bn as its shares fall by half
blurb: SK Hynix will spend $720bn to build what it calls the world's largest network of memory factories, starting with a 50-storey Yongin fab due to begin production in February. The bet lands as investors sour on the AI memory boom, with SK Hynix and Samsung shares down roughly 50% and 34% from June highs even after both posted record earnings.

title: An AI-written article needs no label. Your proofread email gets one
blurb: Anthropic began watermarking all Claude output worldwide on August 2, embedding a secret-key pattern across passages that a detector can spot over 500 to 1,000 words, though it has published neither the algorithm nor a detector. The mark only signals that content "may have been processed by Claude," so it lands on grammar fixes the EU AI Act explicitly exempts while a fully synthetic article can still reach readers unlabelled once a human editor reviews it.

title: Court rejects Apple’s attempt to postpone App Store fee proceedings in Epic Games case [U]
blurb: A federal judge denied Apple's request to pause the Epic Games App Store fee proceedings, giving Apple 24 hours to file its proposed commission.

title: OpenAI plans free ChatGPT Plus year for US college students
blurb: OpenAI is preparing to offer US college students a free year of ChatGPT Plus, gated behind an allowlist of more than 220 campuses and verified through SheerID. The offer positions ChatGPT as an academic layer spanning exam prep, voice-mode rehearsal, and agentic connectors, arriving as a free student year becomes table stakes against Google, Perplexity, and Anthropic.

title: A Pentagon memo tells staff to spend $244m with Palantir. Its subject line is ‘Funding Palantir’
blurb: A Pentagon memo dated 4 August directs staff to buy up to $243.9M in services from Palantir by March 2027 with no competitive bidding, The Register reported. Watchdogs note the memo, titled "Funding Palantir," names no contract vehicle and cites none of the narrow legal grounds under 10 USC 3204 that let a department skip a competition, which the department calls standard practice.

title: Google’s most sophisticated foldable: Pixel 11 Pro Fold
blurb: Google released the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, its most durable Fold yet with a Tensor G6 chip and a new HiLight camera-bar LED indicator.

title: Qualcomm reveals Snapdragon C specs for budget laptops, and Intel could have a serious headache
blurb: Qualcomm revealed Snapdragon C specs for $300 budget laptops, claiming 67% faster on-battery performance than Intel's N250.

title: Claude will begin digitally watermarking marking AI-generated text and images — Anthropic details how it'll comply with the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act
blurb: Anthropic detailed how new Claude models will comply with the EU AI Act's article 50, watermarking generated text by biasing token selection and attaching C2PA provenance certificates to PNG, JPG, and SVG images ahead of the August 2, 2026 deadline. Notably absent is pixel-level image watermarking, which the accompanying Code of Practice requires, leaving Anthropic behind OpenAI and Google, which published their compliance plans earlier.

title: Samsung Foundry updates process roadmap to move 1.4nm node to 2029 — high-NA EUV will enable 1nm-class and smaller nodes in 2030 and beyond
blurb: Samsung Foundry pushed its 1.4nm-class SF1.4 node from 2027 to 2029 and will hold off on High-NA EUV lithography until its 1nm-class SF1A process in 2030. The delay reroutes resources toward refining the 2nm-class SF2 family for better yields and volume, keeping key customers like Tesla, which sourced AI5 and AI6 processors through 2033, supplied on a proven process.

title: Passenger returning from DEF CON 34 spoofs Delta Wi-Fi network while in flight using pentest tool — pilots tell ground crew to alert corporate security after attendee from hacking conference brings the party to the sky
blurb: A DEF CON 34 attendee spoofed a "Delta WiFi Fast" evil-twin network mid-flight using a Wi-Fi Pineapple to phish passengers' Google credentials.

title: Google Puts Gemini at 1 Billion Monthly Users Without Naming Paying Subscribers
blurb: Google said the Gemini app passed 1 billion monthly active users on Aug. 11, making it the fastest product in Google's history to reach that mark and its 14th to do so. The count covers only the Gemini app and web interface, excludes Search and Workspace, and comes with no paid-subscriber figure against Alphabet's 2026 capital-spending forecast of $195B to $205B.

title: Spotify Will Label AI Personas in September and Drop Them From Recommendations
blurb: Spotify will add an AI Persona badge to artist profiles with apparently AI-generated identities starting in mid-September, pulling those accounts from editorial and algorithmic recommendations unless a listener follows them. The move follows AI acts like Enlly Blue racking up 29 million streams on a single track, while at rival Deezer fully AI-generated songs hit nearly 90,000 daily uploads in June, over half the total.

title: Intel Prices $20 Billion Stock Sale at $95, Below Monday's Close
blurb: Intel priced its common stock offering at $95 a share and upsized it to $20 billion, above the $15 billion floated Monday, for roughly $19.7 billion in net proceeds. The 210.5 million new shares dilute existing holders by about 4%, and the filing names only "general corporate purposes" as Intel Foundry booked a $2.09 billion operating loss on just $293 million in external revenue last quarter.

title: OpenAI’s head of ethics leaves less than a year after joining
blurb: OpenAI’s head of ethics departed less than a year after joining, marking another senior exit from the company’s safety and governance ranks. The quick turnover adds to scrutiny of how OpenAI balances rapid commercial expansion against its stated safety commitments, a tension that has driven several high-profile departures over the past two years.

title: Facebook is paying controversial creators to produce rage-bait content
blurb: An ABC News Verify investigation found that Meta directly pays several controversial Australian creators, including a white nationalist with neo-Nazi links and a prominent anti-vaxxer, through Facebook's content monetization programs. Some of the paid content appears to violate Meta's own monetization policies, but the company declined to comment on specific pages and said it is "not Meta's role to police offensiveness.

title: London Underground begins scanning passengers' faces
blurb: British Transport Police expanded its live facial recognition trial to London Underground stations, scanning passengers' faces against watchlists in real time. The rollout follows similar deployments by London's Metropolitan Police and extends biometric surveillance to one of the world's busiest transit systems, intensifying debate over consent and accuracy in public-space monitoring.

title: Making holograms with a pen plotter
blurb: A developer used a pen plotter to draw reflective etch-holograms, curved scratch patterns that steer a bright highlight across a surface as the viewing angle changes. The post explains the optics intuitively, starting with the moving glint on an oil-smudged phone screen, then automates the precise arc-drawing that hand-etching makes tedious.

title: This Iranian Malware Has No C2 Server to Block. The Command Channel Is a Meeting Invite in Your Own Calendar
blurb: Group-IB disclosed HollowGraph, Iranian malware with no C2 server that hides commands in the victim's own Microsoft 365 calendar.

title: Flock Cameras Can Track Every Car in America. Police Love Them. Citizens Don’t.
blurb: Flock's automated license-plate readers now blanket thousands of American communities, letting police search a near-nationwide log of where and when specific cars have traveled. A New York Times report finds the surveillance draws bipartisan unease in Texas, where liberals and conservatives alike object to cameras tracking their movements without warrants or meaningful oversight.

title: Apple wins temporary Supreme Court pause in Epic Games proceedings
blurb: The Supreme Court granted Apple a temporary administrative stay pausing lower-court proceedings in the Epic Games case until Thursday, halting a deadline that required Apple to propose what commission it should charge on App Store external-payment purchases. Justice Elena Kagan issued the 24-hour pause while the Court weighs Apple's request for a longer stay tied to its pending appeal of the contempt ruling over the 27% fee it imposed on outside links.

title: CoreWeave coasts to a solid earnings beat, sending its stock higher after-hours
blurb: CoreWeave beat Q2 estimates with revenue up 112% to $2.58B, sending shares up 14% after-hours on a $104B backlog.

title: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workstation edition price doubles, as NVIDIA launches new AI model
blurb: NVIDIA doubled the price of its RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition to $16,000, citing rising memory costs across the industry. The move coincides with the launch of Nemotron 3.5, a lightweight model expanding the company's AI portfolio as it raises hardware prices.

title: Memory maker CXMT overtakes Tencent to become China's most valuable company 17 days after its IPO — now worth $524 billion
blurb: CXMT overtook Tencent to become China's most valuable company at $524 billion, just 17 days after its $8.6 billion Shanghai IPO. The DRAM maker, which holds 7.67% of the global memory market and signed multibillion-dollar server deals with Tencent and ByteDance, climbed past Tencent as the internet giant fell on news of a 176% jump in AI infrastructure spending.

title: Lovable: The $13bn power of word of mouth
blurb: Lovable raised $400M in Series C at a $13.3bn valuation, doubling its December 2025 valuation as projects grew from 25M to 60M.

title: Nebius shares jump 34% on continued AI infrastructure demand
blurb: Nebius Group shares closed 34% higher after Q2 revenue surged 454% year-over-year to $582.3 million, beating consensus and driven by four data center deals averaging over $1 billion each. The AI-cloud provider signed contracts with Cohere and Reflection AI, narrowed its quarterly loss 64% to $33.2 million, and spent $5.7 billion on capex it expects to recoup within about two years.

title: PBS broadcaster loses access to 50TB of data comprising 70 years of TV history after contracted cloud storage vendor goes defunct — public TV channel sues Iron Mountain data center, which hosts archival materials, to ensure preservation
blurb: Nine PBS lost access to 50TB of archival data spanning 70 years of programming after its cloud storage vendor, Open Source Storage, went defunct and cut off retrieval this year. A Colorado court ruled the station is entitled to its data, and it is now pressing Iron Mountain, which physically hosts the archive, to preserve and hand over the files.

title: Intel CEO hints at return to the memory business — says market is ripe for innovation, hints at stacking memory and CPU
blurb: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan signaled the company may re-enter the memory business, calling new memory architectures a strategic "pet project" and pointing to CPU-memory stacking as a promising direction. The remarks follow Intel's hiring of former SK Hynix chief Seok-Hee Lee and a patent for XBM, an HBM alternative that drops the silicon interposer, as 3D NAND and DRAM makers post record profits.

title: Independent bookstores in Europe receive suspicious orders for thousands of books, prompting fears they'll be destroyed to train AI — sellers believe acquisitions are part of AI tech companies’ push to get more data
blurb: Independent bookstores across Europe are receiving suspicious bulk orders for thousands of obscure titles, which sellers suspect are AI companies harvesting books to feed training datasets. The pattern follows reports that firms are shredding millions of purchased books with destructive scanners to digitize them, adding a physical-supply dimension to ongoing lawsuits over pirated text like Meta's torrenting of 82TB of books.

title: Two undersea cables reportedly damaged off the coast of Perth following suspicious vessel activity — company CEO says faults happened ‘straight after each other and in close proximity'
blurb: Two undersea cables off Perth reported near-simultaneous shunt faults after suspicious vessel activity, and Australian police are investigating possible sabotage.

title: AST SpaceMobile integrates, tests network in Europe as BlueBird satellites launch successfully
blurb: AST SpaceMobile began testing its satellite network integration across eight European countries with operators including Orange, Vodafone, and Deutsche Telekom, following the successful launch of its BlueBird 11, 12, and 13 low-Earth orbit satellites. The BlueBirds support peak rates up to 200 Mb/s and connect standard smartphones directly, positioning AST against SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon's Leo in the direct-to-device market.

title: Go is an ideal language for AI-assisted software engineering
blurb: Google argues that Go is well-suited to AI-assisted development because what matters now is reviewing and maintaining generated code, not the speed of writing it. The post ties Go's opinionated simplicity, uniform tooling, and long-term compatibility guarantees to a workflow where AI generates large amounts of code and humans verify and own the architecture.

title: New TONTOU CPU Attack Bypasses Spectre v2 Fixes to Leak Linux Password Hashes
blurb: MIT researchers disclosed TONTOU, an attack that defeats the neutralization-based Spectre v2 mitigations (Intel's eIBRS and AMD's Safe RET) by re-poisoning the CPU's branch predictor in the gap between when its state is sanitized and when the victim branch uses it. Using an Interrupt Injection primitive, unprivileged programs can schedule timer interrupts during kernel execution to leak arbitrary memory, including hashed Linux passwords.

title: Spotify's new ‘skip' button could end the podcast business as we know it
blurb: Spotify is testing a feature that lets some users skip through podcast ads, promos, and filler, as long as those ads aren't sold directly by Spotify. The change threatens shows that rely on direct-sold advertising and reinforces a two-tiered system where Spotify-sold ads are unskippable while publishers' own ads can be bypassed, pushing the platform further toward premium subscriptions.

title: Rocket Lab Unveils GHOST on a Record Quarter
blurb: Rocket Lab introduced GHOST, a container-based launch system that packs rockets, ground support, and range control into standard shipping containers to enable orbital and suborbital launches from anywhere, with an operational debut planned for 2027 in Kodiak, Alaska. The announcement accompanied record Q2 revenue of $234M, up 62% year over year, and a backlog of $2.36B alongside more than $1B in new launch and defense contracts.

title: Twitch feeds your streams to Amazon's AI unless you tell it to stop
blurb: Twitch now feeds users' streams into Amazon's AI models by default, requiring an opt-out in account settings to stop it.

title: Elon Musk says xAI will increase data center capacity 7x by 2027 — targeting 10 gigawatts of compute, up to $500 billion in revenue by the end of next year
blurb: Elon Musk told employees that xAI will grow its data center power capacity roughly sevenfold to 10GW by the end of 2027, up from 1.4GW across its Memphis and Southaven sites today. He projected the buildout could generate $300B to $500B in annual revenue, pricing compute at $30 to $50 per watt, though the target lands as SpaceX's valuation fell by nearly $570B in under two months.

title: The web’s newest weapon against AI scrapers is a font
blurb: ShieldFont uses ligatures to serve readers a clean webpage while feeding AI scrapers a nonsensical, word-swapped version of the underlying HTML.

title: Google launches five new Pixel devices, array of Gemini Intelligence features
blurb: Google launched five new Pixel devices, headlined by the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, all running the Tensor G6 chip and upgraded Gemini Intelligence features.

title: Can Agents Use a Computer Yet? We've Got the Data
blurb: a16z benchmarks how well AI agents complete real computer-use tasks, with the underlying data on where they still fail.

title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
blurb: Two malicious LiteLLM releases, versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, sat on PyPI for about 40 minutes on March 24 carrying code that harvested cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords from systems that installed them. CloudSEK now maps potential exposure to more than 2,500 organizations, including NVIDIA, Cisco, Deloitte, and Volkswagen, and both it and LiteLLM urge affected parties to rotate credentials rather than wait for proof of misuse.

title: Testing ads in ChatGPT
blurb: OpenAI expanded ChatGPT Ads to the United Kingdom, Mexico, Brazil, Japan, and South Korea, moving the pilot beyond its initial U.S. test and earlier Canada, Australia, and New Zealand rollout. Ads appear only for logged-in adult users on the Free and Go tiers, do not influence ChatGPT's answers, and keep conversations private from advertisers, with paid tiers remaining ad-free.

title: Nvidia’s Risky Business
blurb: Ben Thompson draws a parallel between Nvidia and Jay Cooke, whose retail-bond financing of the Northern Pacific Railway collapsed into the Panic of 1873. The argument is that Nvidia is increasingly underwriting demand for its own chips through circular deals and vendor financing, taking on the same downstream risk that felled Cooke when capital needs proved endless and credit tightened. The historical rhyme is the warning: infrastructure booms funded by their own supplier tend to end badly.

title: DeepSeek Harness
blurb: DeepSeek AI released DeepSeek Harness (dsh), an open-source agent harness built on a plugin-everything architecture powered by Cordis, a runtime based on the spatiotemporal composability paradigm. It runs from a local Web UI via npx and is currently in developer preview, with the maintainers warning of compatibility-breaking changes as the project iterates.

title: What sort of maths are LLMs good at?
blurb: Timothy Gowers examines what kinds of mathematics current LLMs are actually good at, prompted by OpenAI's recent claim to have solved ten major open problems, including the first construction of a non-sofic group and superexponential growth for a multicolour Ramsey number. He notes that the most famous solved problems have mostly involved finding counterexamples rather than constructing proofs, and treats the piece as a snapshot of capabilities in early August 2026 that he expects to age quickly.

title: Sources: Anthropic's investors expect it to float at a $2T+ valuation in an October IPO and to hit $100B to $120B in annualized revenue by the end of 2026 (Financial Times)
blurb: Anthropic's investors expect the company to go public at a $2T+ valuation in an October IPO, according to sources cited by the Financial Times. The same sources project Anthropic will reach $100B to $120B in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, a sharp acceleration from its current run rate.

title: H3-metal – Native MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple Silicon
blurb: H3-metal is a native MiniMax-H3 inference engine for Apple Silicon that runs prompt-to-video and prompt-to-audio generation directly on Metal, without Python or external ML frameworks. It supports first/last-frame conditioning and ordered Ref2VA image, video, and audio references, and ships an Iris-style interactive session that keeps BF16 conditioning and the video decoder in memory to skip re-encoding across seeds.

title: Prompt Injections for Defense
blurb: Researchers at Tracebit found that embedding prompt injections alongside passwords and cryptographic keys in AWS often shut down attacks from AI hacking agents. The planted prompts order the attacking LLM to perform a guardrail-forbidden action, such as detailing anthrax production or referencing Tank Man, at which point the model refuses to continue and abandons its task. The technique, called context bombing, only works against agents with guardrails, so locally run models without them will leave attackers unaffected.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.6-Cyber with Reduced Safeguards for Exploit Development
blurb: OpenAI released GPT-5.6-Cyber, a cybersecurity-focused model built on GPT-5.6 Sol that is trained for vulnerability research, exploit-chain development, and incident response while reducing refusals on higher-risk, dual-use tasks. Available through a new Daybreak Red tier for authorized security testing, the model completes 95% of advanced cyber requests versus 1.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol and already surfaced CVE-2026-15903, a high-severity V8 flaw.

title: Lovable raises $400m backed by EU’s Scaleup Fund
blurb: Lovable raised $400M at a $13.3B valuation, led by existing investor Menlo Ventures and the EU-backed Scaleup Fund managed by EQT. The Stockholm-based vibe-coding platform, founded in 2024, hit $500M in ARR in June and had reached a $6.6B valuation in its December Series B, roughly doubling its price in eight months.

title: How Organizations Use AI: Evidence from ChatGPT
