Released under Apache-2.0, it packages the debugging knowledge from operating OHTTP at millions of requests per second behind products like Apple Private Relay and Microsoft Edge Secure Network VPN.

title: GitSkills: A Dataset of Agent Skills on GitHub
blurb: GitSkills is a dataset of 3,797,117 SKILL.md files collected from 282,200 public GitHub repositories in July 2026, capturing how developers write, reuse, and maintain the agent-skill format Anthropic introduced in October 2025. The authors deduplicate to 1,877,981 distinct contents, enrich one representative per group with parsed front matter, folder contents, repo metadata, and partial commit history, and ship it as a single SQLite file for research on adoption, reuse, authorship, maintenance, and security.

title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Delivers Fast, Accurate Specialized Task Execution for Long-Running Agents
blurb: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters built for the high-volume execution layer of long-running agents. It ships with speculative decoding and harness-optimized training for tools like OpenClaw, alongside NeMo Switchyard, a routing library that sends each task to the cheapest model that can handle it.

title: TDD inside the agent loop - theater or actual value?
blurb: Martin Fowler's team ran an exploratory eval on whether forcing a coding agent to follow TDD fully inside its own loop actually improves output, generating small, medium, and large greenfield tasks with Sonnet 4.6 and grading them with Opus. The result was no discernible quality gain, with non-TDD solutions occasionally ranked slightly higher on design and test quality and no meaningful difference in mutation scores.

title: Breaking the WAL
blurb: Antithesis reproduced SQLite's WAL-Reset bug, a data race that lurked in the Write-Ahead Logging subsystem since 2010 and that SQLite's own developers could never trigger organically. Using Claude to instrument version 3.51.2 with generic assertions like "no lost committed writes" and running concurrent writes and checkpoints, their deterministic simulator caught it in 15 minutes, then came back green against the patched 3.51.3.

title: Show HN: Woxi - Open-source Mathematica / Wolfram Language reimplementation
blurb: Woxi is an open-source reimplementation of the Wolfram Language and Mathematica that ships as a Jupyter kernel. Install it locally with `woxi install-kernel`, or run notebooks in the browser through the bundled JupyterLite instance with no local setup required.

title: Agentic Code Quality
blurb: Addy Osmani argues that code review no longer scales as the primary quality check once agents generate hundreds of thousands of changes a day, so quality now depends on the constraints you wrap around them. He frames quality gates such as unit and property tests, mutation testing, and complexity metrics as the deterministic loop that decides whether an agent's proposal is safe, correct, and scoped enough to ship.

title: Total Recall at What Cost? Benchmarking the Serving Cost of Agentic Memory Systems
blurb: This paper benchmarks the serving cost of three agentic memory systems (Mem0, Hindsight, and Mastra Observational Memory) against a rolling window and full-transcript resubmission across two backbones and conversations up to 400 turns. Cost can't be predicted from conversation length alone, break-even against full transcript ranges from tens of turns to never within 400, and no system wins on both cost and accuracy.

title: Deeply buried 16-year-old SQLite bug caused last year's Tailscale outages
blurb: A 16-year-old bug in SQLite's query planner was traced as the root cause of Tailscale's outages last year, surfacing only under a specific index-usage pattern that had gone unhit for over a decade. The write-up walks through how Tailscale's engineers narrowed an intermittent failure down to the buried SQLite path and coordinated the upstream fix.

title: ChatGPT Desktop (Codex Desktop) for Linux
blurb: OpenAI released a Linux build of its Codex desktop app, extending the agentic coding client that already runs in ChatGPT, an IDE extension, and a CLI. The desktop app pairs with built-in worktrees and cloud environments to run agents in parallel across projects, and adds Skills for encoding team standards and scheduled background tasks like issue triage, CI/CD, and PR review.

title: CodeRabbit lands $143M at $1.5B valuation as AI-generated code surges
blurb: CodeRabbit raised $143M in Series C funding at a $1.5B valuation, co-led by Atomico and Smash Capital, less than a year after its $60M Series B. The AI code review startup now runs over two million reviews a week for 17,000+ customers including NVIDIA and BMW, and is expanding into change management with Triage, Change Stack, and CodeRabbit Security.

title: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash: Better, faster, at a quarter of the cost
blurb: Microsoft released MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, its small coding model now serving in GitHub Copilot, at a quarter of the cost of the 1.0 version from June. The update posts a 22% gain on Terminal-Bench 2.1 in Copilot CLI and a 15% improvement on .NET tasks, while streaming tokens 25% faster and using 25% fewer tokens per task.

title: Understanding the Architecture of Coding Agents: An Exploratory Study Using a Research Prototype
blurb: This paper documents the internal architecture of coding agents and introduces Ark, a minimal open-source agent that preserves the essential components while stripping everything else for teaching and research. Running gpt-5.4-mini, Ark solved 8 of 10 tasks on the accompanying ArkBench suite with modest token consumption, and the authors compare its design against state-of-the-art agents using a recent architectural taxonomy.

title: Message your other Claude Code sessions
blurb: Claude Code v2.1.224 adds cross-session messaging, letting one session hand a finding, status, or decision to another through the new ListAgents and SendMessage tools without you copy-pasting between terminals. It works on macOS and Linux with no setup once sessions meet the version requirement, covers parallel worktrees and long-running jobs, and can reply to sessions on other machines though cross-machine exchanges must be started locally.

title: We Deleted Two Skills That Tried to Help
blurb: The team deleted two agent skills after a Forge release postmortem showed both quietly expanded a bounded "ship one change" task past any stable boundary. JFDI turned an operator's "approve everything" prompt into open-ended production authority with no stop condition, pushing main and applying migrations through cascading platform defects, while Maintainability Guardrails expanded what ordinary coding work appeared to require by attaching broad hardening obligations.

title: How and Why Netflix Built a Real-Time Distributed Graph: Part 3 — Querying the graph with gRPC execution API
blurb: The third installment of Netflix's distributed graph series details the gRPC-based execution API that serves queries against the graph, covering how the engine plans traversals, batches subqueries, and streams results back to callers. The design favors a typed gRPC contract over GraphQL at the storage layer, trading schema flexibility for tighter control over execution cost and predictable latency under Netflix's real-time read load.

title: Modular's Mojo programming language hits 1.0 milestone
blurb: Modular released version 1.0 of Mojo, its Python-superset language aimed at high-performance AI and systems code, marking the first stable release after years of preview. Developers are still waiting on the promised open source compiler to clear up uncertainty following Qualcomm's acquisition of Modular, which leaves the language's long-term governance and portability an open question.

title: GraphAlignCoder: Aligning Program and Proof Graphs for Code Generation
blurb: GraphAlignCoder is a training framework that injects formal correctness structure into code LLMs by aligning a program's control-and-dependence graph with a proof-flow graph extracted from Lean proof traces. It beats CodeRL across benchmarks, raising the solved count from 38 to 50 on LiveCodeBench v6 and 16 to 23 on BigCodeBench Hard, with ablations showing the verification-to-code consolidation step is what drives robust cross-benchmark transfer.

title: Canva redesigns session revocation for 100M active sessions
blurb: Canva rebuilt its session revocation system to handle hundreds of millions of active sessions by storing revocations as compact 16-byte binary records in Amazon S3 rather than hammering MySQL, using immutable objects and conditional writes as coordination primitives. Gateways download 30-minute S3 chunks via conditional GETs into sorted in-memory indexes, cutting the revocation cache footprint by 87.5% while eliminating the coordinated database load that hit MySQL during deployments.

title: MergirafSemi: A Language-Agnostic Semistructured Merge Tool
blurb: MergirafSemi is a language-agnostic semistructured merge tool that uses lightweight Concrete Syntax Trees to guide merges while falling back to line-based merging inside regions like Java method bodies. In an empirical study across multiple languages, it cut spurious conflicts versus unstructured tools and matched a language-specific semistructured tool's accuracy, with lower runtime overhead and more robust execution in most common scenarios.

title: Cursor prepares to launch Origin platform for code reviews
blurb: Cursor is preparing to open Origin, its Graphite-built code review platform, beyond the closed partner beta, with interface strings pointing to a "Cursor Review" rollout as early as this week. The system adds an automated pull request pipeline that pings developers only when their judgment is needed, targeting the review bottleneck that stalls teams running fleets of background agents rather than the generation step.

title: Microsoft releases MAI-Code-1.1-Flash coding model to better compete with Chinese models
blurb: Microsoft released MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, a coding model that replaces MAI-Code-1-Flash and improves on it across development tasks, including a 22% gain on Terminal-Bench 2.1. The release positions Microsoft's in-house coding models against faster-moving Chinese open-weight competitors.

title: Can software factories actually work?
blurb: PostHog examines whether "software factories" — pipelines where agents pull tickets, build PRs, and ship via CI/CD with minimal human review — can scale, weighing HumanLayer CEO Dex Horthy's viral argument that they never will against real-world adoption at Ramp, Cursor, Uber, and PostHog itself. The post frames autonomy as a spectrum, noting PostHog's agents write roughly 70% of its PRs while humans still skim at least 80% of them.

title: Do Influence Tactics Matter? Investigating Prompt Framing Effects in LLM Code Generation
blurb: This paper runs the first large-scale test of whether psychology-based prompt framings, operationalized from Yukl and Falbe's eight influence tactics, change LLM code output across five open-weight models on LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench Verified. Framings that emphasized urgency were associated with lower functional correctness and weaker security, measured across four quality dimensions including maintainability.

title: Harnessing LLMs for Document-Guided Fuzzing of Python Libraries
blurb: VistaFuzz uses a locally served open-source LLM to extract per-parameter constraints and inter-parameter dependencies from API docs, then generates fuzzing inputs that satisfy both. Tested across 7,718 APIs in twelve Python libraries, it found that disabling dependency resolution drops the valid-input rate from above 95% to 31.6-52.8% on the 40% of APIs with inter-parameter relationships, and it surfaced 74 issues, 43 developer-confirmed and 29 fixed.

title: The Devil Is in the Interface: Evaluating How Tool Architecture Shapes Coding Agent Behavior
blurb: This paper studies how tool architecture, not just tool capability, shapes coding agent behavior across 11,700 repository-level issue-fixing trajectories. Holding the underlying information and actions fixed, structured low-level interfaces improved cross-attempt consistency by up to 4.7x, natural-language search raised access to relevant files by over 11%, and Python CodeAct-style interfaces matched task performance with 41.6% fewer steps and 56.3% lower token usage.

title: Show HN: Git-knife – Edit commit messages, authors, and dates like a spreadsheet
blurb: git-knife is a desktop GUI for editing git commit metadata directly, including message, author name/email, and the author and committer dates that GUIs like GitKraken, Fork, and Sublime Merge treat as immutable. It shells out to the system git CLI and rebuilds commits with git commit-tree, reusing each commit's original tree so file contents never change, and supports bulk regex edits with an automatic backup ref before every rewrite.

title: Why you might want to build your WebApp in Canvas instead of HTML
blurb: The author explains why performance-critical web apps like Google Docs, Miro, and Canva render their core surfaces on Canvas rather than the DOM, trading the browser's built-in layout, event handling, and reflow for a bare drawing API. Canvas skips HTML parsing, style computation, and reflow to gain speed and full rendering control for infinite workspaces and zoomable grids, at the cost of reimplementing text, accessibility, and hit-testing yourself.

title: Relying on Go
blurb: Solod is a systems language for C and Go developers that is literally a subset of Go, reusing its syntax highlighting, LSP, linters, package management, and much of its standard library code verbatim rather than trying to fix Go's mistakes. The trade-off is that Go's tooling doesn't know Solod is a subset, so it won't flag full-Go features that Solod doesn't support, and the language adds manual memory management with explicit allocators.

title: Vertical slices, their ownership and external dependencies
blurb: The author argues that vertical slices, modules, and bounded contexts get conflated, and that treating every application area as a fully autonomous bounded context sets the separation bar so high that any dependency between slices looks like a violation. The fix is defining what a slice does when it needs something external, since "minimise coupling" means non-zero, not the myth that slices can never share code or read what another slice wrote.

title: Towards Automated Domain Model Extraction from Source Code using Heuristics and Open-Source LLMs
blurb: This paper introduces a method for extracting domain models from source code using locally deployable open-source LLMs, combining structural and semantic heuristics with iterative reasoning to work around small context windows. By progressively analyzing ranked subsets of code elements rather than requiring full-system context, the approach hits high F1-scores across ten projects while staying runnable on-premise for privacy-sensitive industrial codebases.

title: Perry Mason in: The Case of the Drifting Timer
blurb: A four-iteration walkthrough of building a production-grade reactive clock in Vue 3, from setInterval memory leak to scope-safe cleanup.

title: From Finding to Fixing: Reducing maintainer burden with automated patches
blurb: Google connected OSS-Fuzz to CodeMender, DeepMind's code-security agent, so that a fuzzer crash now feeds directly into an automated pipeline that finds the root cause and produces a validated patch. The system leans on fuzzing's near-zero false-positive rate to avoid the noise of agentic scanners, then has CodeMender explore code paths in parallel and validate that each patch preserves existing functionality before delivering it to maintainers.

title: How Cursor Router chooses the right model for the task
blurb: Cursor Router picks a model per turn using Compass, a learned complexity predictor, plus a task taxonomy trained on live developer traffic rather than benchmark scores. Its Auto Intelligence mode now delivers above Fable-level user satisfaction at 68% lower cost, while Auto Balance outperforms Opus 4.8 at 41% lower cost with a slight satisfaction gain.

title: Testing Deep Learning Library APIs via Cross-Framework Differential Fuzzing
blurb: Xamt applies cross-framework differential fuzzing to deep learning library APIs, testing groups of equivalent operations across seven libraries rather than relying on the CPU-GPU differential oracles that miss backend-consistent bugs. It built 676 execution-validated groups covering 2,563 matched APIs and surfaced 72 reproduced discrepancies, including 4 crashes; 25 have been confirmed by developers and 23 already fixed.

title: Hax – a minimalist, terminal-native coding agent written in C
blurb: Hax is a terminal-native coding agent shipped as a single native C binary with a small dependency set, starting instantly and using just a few MB of RAM to leave room for local LLMs. It auto-discovers local model runtimes like llama.cpp as first-class providers, preserves native scrollback by redrawing only the streaming line, and deliberately omits plugin runtimes, IDE panels, and MCP marketplaces that other agents build.

title: Scaling an Agentic Coding SDK: What Concurrency Actually Costs
blurb: Scaling a batch dependency fixer built on the GitHub Copilot SDK from a sequential loop to a five-worker pool cut a 30-repository run from roughly 46 minutes to about 12. The author's key reframe is that a Copilot session is a long-lived workload, not an HTTP request, so each concurrent agent needs an isolated workspace, reliable cleanup, resource and rate limits, durable job ownership, and safe retries before the parallelism pays off.

title: The Role Specialization Model (RSM): Coordinating LLM-Based Tools in Agentic Software Development - An Exploratory Case Study
blurb: This paper coordinates three LLM tools—the Antigravity agentic IDE, Gemini CLI, and a local Qwen Code runner on Ollama—under a Role Specialization Model that assigns each a distinct function while building a Python climate-visualization desktop app. The case study documents where agents deviated from their planned roles, the prompt-hardening used to correct them, and an ISO/IEC 25010 quality assessment, concluding that explicit role coordination helps but still needs careful context management and human verification.

title: Metabase SQL Zero-Day Attacks Could Have Wide Blast Radius
blurb: Metabase disclosed a maximum-severity SQL-injection zero-day (CVSS 10, still no CVE) that let attackers gain remote admin access to instances, alter configuration, and steal credentials for every connected database. Metabase Cloud customers were auto-patched, but self-hosted deployments running version 1.58 or later with the /api/session/reset_password endpoint exposed to the internet remain exploitable and should lock that endpoint down immediately.

title: Open-sourcing Metals v2: Databricks’ Java and Scala language server for multi‑million line codebases
blurb: Databricks open-sourced Metals v2, extending the Scala language server with first-class Java support and scaling it to handle its 26M-line Bazel monorepo, and shipped it for Cursor, VS Code, and Neovim. The work let the company pair lightweight editors with coding agents instead of IntelliJ, and by July 2026 92% of weekly active IDE users opened Cursor versus 12% for IntelliJ.

title: Taking AUTO CDC to the next level: Solving the hardest real-world use cases
blurb: Databricks extended AUTO CDC in Spark Declarative Pipelines to handle bitemporal change data capture, tracking business time and system time as two independent axes so teams can reconstruct both what a fact was and what their systems believed at any past date. Each target table gets four managed columns and rewrites affected history when late or out-of-order corrections arrive, no hand-written MERGE logic required. The capability targets audit regimes like SEC Rule 17a-4, and is landing in open-source Apache Spark 4.2.

title: How We Pushed CDC into Postgres
blurb: Snowflake engineers detailed how they rebuilt Postgres change data capture from the ground up for Snowflake Postgres, replacing the usual pull-based logical decoding pipeline with a push model. The new data mirroring feature, now in public preview, pushes committed changes directly from Postgres into Apache Iceberg tables in transactional batches, then applies them to Snowflake serverlessly with low lag and transactional consistency. The pitch is one button instead of the fragile, high-cost replication tooling most teams stitch together themselves.

title: Looker’s semantic layer governs Gemini Enterprise data for user trust
blurb: Google integrated Looker's governed semantic layer into Gemini Enterprise, letting Looker analysts publish conversational agents natively via the Agent-to-Agent protocol so users query structured metrics and unstructured documents in one chat interface. The semantic layer supplies codified join logic and metric definitions to constrain NL2SQL, giving deterministic answers instead of the inconsistent numbers and hallucinations that raw schema-guessing produces.

title: Electric joins Databricks to bring WASM Postgres to AI agent sandboxes
blurb: Databricks acquired Electric, maker of PGlite (a WASM Postgres that runs inside an agent sandbox, browser tab, or device) and a real-time sync engine that reconciles that local state back to a central Lakebase. The deal extends Databricks' Postgres reach from the lakehouse to the edge, giving each agent its own low-latency local database while keeping a governed source of truth in the cloud.

title: Accelerate PostgreSQL migrations using Gemini in Database Migration Service
blurb: Google added AI-assisted code conversion powered by Gemini to Database Migration Service, translating Oracle PL/SQL and SQL Server T-SQL stored procedures, triggers, and functions into PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL inside the Cloud console. The feature targets the "last mile" of migrations, where hundreds of proprietary routines usually demand months of manual dual-dialect rewriting before a move to open-source Postgres or AlloyDB can finish.

title: Databricks closed a $5B funding round at a $190B valuation, six months after raising $5B at a $134B valuation, and says it has crossed $7B in revenue run rate (Samantha Subin/CNBC)
blurb: Databricks raised $5B at a $190B valuation, six months after a $5B round valued it at $134B, and says it has crossed $7B in annualized revenue run rate. The 42% valuation jump in half a year signals investors are still betting on Databricks as the consolidation point for the lakehouse and AI-workload stack, ahead of a long-rumored IPO.

title: BigQuery expands data transfers with direct Iceberg ingestion
blurb: BigQuery Data Transfer Service added direct ingestion from GCS, S3, and Azure Blob Storage into Apache Iceberg managed tables in preview, alongside new MCP server, SQL Server, Shopify, and Klaviyo connectors. The Iceberg piece matters most: it lets teams keep object storage as the source of truth for multi-cloud, multi-engine access while still using BigQuery's performance tuning, without hand-built ETL.

title: Automate data monitoring and root-cause analysis with Looker Agentic Workflows
blurb: Google added Looker Agentic Workflows in preview for version 26.08, using background agents to turn natural-language prompts like "notify me if average order value exceeds $1,000" into continuous metric monitors that run Key Driver Analysis and deliver root-cause summaries to Slack or email. The move pushes BI past threshold alerts into automated diagnosis, with admin-level oversight to review or disable workflows across the instance.

title: Breaking the WAL
blurb: Antithesis reproduced SQLite's WAL-Reset bug in 15 minutes using a generic concurrent write-and-checkpoint workload and standard database assertions like "no lost committed writes" and "database not corrupt." The data race had gone undetected since 2010 because it never reproduced organically. The lesson for data teams: the simplest workloads often surface the hardest bugs, and deterministic simulation testing can catch races that manual reproduction never will.

title: Guided Table Retrieval for Structured Data Search
blurb: This paper introduces guided table retrieval, a four-phase pipeline for answering natural language questions over structured databases by identifying relevant tables and inferring their joins. Instead of leaning on a single end-to-end LLM, it splits the work into deterministic hash-based grounding, join-graph exploration, LLM disambiguation, and algorithmic merging into minimal join trees. The authors report 94% precision on BIRD-DEV and 70% on the enterprise-scale BEAVER benchmark, outputting exact join trees that downstream query compilers can consume directly.

title: Time to Move on: Querying without Nulls and Bags
blurb: This paper argues that SQL's tolerance of nulls and bags (duplicate-laden, non-normalized relations) is an avoidable mistake, not a necessary evil. Drawing on their work building Rel, a language for end-to-end relational programming, the authors show a query language can run on fully normalized relations with set semantics, dropping both the "billion dollar mistake" of nulls and Codd's corrupted relations. They contend the usual justifications for keeping them collapse under scrutiny, and outline what a null-free, set-based language enables.

title: An Extended Tutorial and Vocabulary for Relational Language Design in an Era of AI-Assisted Query Generation
blurb: This 3-hour tutorial paper argues that as queries are increasingly written by machines and read by humans, the relevant question for relational language design is no longer expressive power but readability and revisability across SQL, dataframe, pipeline, graph, and functional notations. Using Abstract Relational Calculus and Relational Diagrams as reference representations, the authors build a vocabulary for comparing how languages express the same intent, extending it to recursive path queries, nested relations, and problems beyond PTIME.

title: Reverse Migration of Cloud Applications to On-premises
blurb: Diel, a reverse-migration tool from the Tursio team, automates moving cloud applications back to on-premises environments for regulated industries that can't deploy in the cloud. It combines simulate, replicate, and delegate strategies to transform managed cloud services into on-prem equivalents, resolving the develop-in-cloud, ship-on-prem paradox that stretches release cycles. The team reports keeping Tursio AI's cloud and on-prem builds in sync with stable releases every three weeks.

title: Enabling Differentiated QoS Degradation for Replicated Databases under Failures
blurb: This paper tackles what happens to a replicated database when you can't just spin up replacement replicas after a failure. The authors present PLB, a PostgreSQL JDBC middleware load balancer that reassigns healthy replicas into Premium, Mixed, and Freemium roles under fail-stop failures, keeping the pool shared while preserving service-class differentiation. Against shared round-robin routing, it holds 26-28 more percentage points of median Premium goodput and cuts Premium p95 latency by 18.2%.

title: Plaintext Recovery Against Post-Filtering Access Control
blurb: This paper shows that post-filtering access control in databases leaks far more than prior work assumed. Row- and document-level security let untrusted queries run over all data before redacting private rows, and the authors turn that into full plaintext recovery. They exploit RLS timing side-channels in PostgreSQL and DLS scoring in Elasticsearch, using range, prefix, and conjunctive predicates to binary-search unknown values into complete records and approximate documents.

title: Building Tactile UX: Honoring Intentional Design With Lottie
blurb: Isadora Agency's team built Stress Release, a browser-based squeeze toy, without a physics engine, driving every tactile reaction through Lottie's native state API, DOM manipulation, and distance-based math instead of Matter.js or WebGL. The writeup argues that physics engines produce plausible motion while animators produce intentional motion, and that deterministic frame control (down to a 181-frame mega-squeeze) is the right call when hand-crafted keyframes need to survive the interaction layer.

title: The new 7UP rebrand is bound to be contentious
blurb: 7UP unveiled its biggest identity overhaul in 15 years, pairing a soft retro wordmark and lime-forward palette with a reformulated "Lime Lemon" recipe, just three years after its last rebrand. Keurig Dr Pepper is chasing citrus-leaning Gen Z and Gen Alpha drinkers, but the inverted "lime lemon" naming breaks a conventional word order that will likely draw as much attention as the visuals.

title: Has the world been too harsh on Disney's Hexed?
blurb: A FramebyFrame breakdown on X pushes back against the pile-on over Disney's Hexed, arguing the trailer still demonstrates classic animation principles like opposing directional movement, lead-and-follow, and beat-and-hold timing that keep the action readable. The analysis is a useful reminder that technical animation craft and the reception of a film's design, character, and story are separate judgments that critics often conflate.

title: The CSS hack that extends your website on iOS Safari
blurb: This tutorial shows how to style the areas iOS Safari extends behind the status bar and tab bar by setting a `body` background-color that bleeds past your header and footer, with a CodePen demo. The technique closes the default white gap at the top and bottom of a mobile page, a small polish detail most sites leave unaddressed.

title: Heatherwick Studio adjusts design of Louisville waterfront park to "restore buzz"
blurb: Heatherwick Studio released updated designs for Belvedere, a park and event space in Louisville, Kentucky, with sections built atop a highway overpass to reconnect Downtown with the Ohio River waterfront. The revision reworks the 1970s-era site to "restore buzz," adding new landscaping and gathering areas across the elevated deck that spans the interstate below.

title: Kii uses local limestone and colourful "melting" stools for SR Ice Cream Miyakojima
blurb: Kii's SR Ice Cream shop on Miyakojima pairs a local limestone counter, a pink ceiling, and colorful "melting" stools.

title: The Signal Rail: A Deterministic Motion Grammar for Communicating Conversational Agent State in Terminal Interfaces
blurb: This paper proposes the Signal Rail, a one-row terminal status instrument that gives a conversational agent's motion channel a grammar, mapping states like listening, thinking, and executing to distinct kinetic rules rather than relying on color or a single alive-or-not blink. Its four principles, spatial semantics, one motion rule per state, deterministic golden-frame-testable rendering, and no invented progress, make it a rigorous reference for anyone designing honest loading and status animation.

title: What does the sale of ArtStation and Sketchfab mean for digital artists?
blurb: Epic Games sold ArtStation and Sketchfab to KitBash, the company behind KitBash3D and Greyscalegorilla, five years after acquiring both platforms in 2021. The move lets Epic concentrate on Unreal Engine 6 and Fortnite while handing ArtStation's 10 million-user portfolio community to an owner promising to integrate it with production 3D asset libraries, leaving artists to watch how marketplace terms and portfolio hosting shift.

title: Player Perceptions of Generative AI in Games: A Steam Review Analysis
blurb: Analyzing 508,192 Steam reviews, researchers found that games disclosing generative AI use draw lower recommendation rates and more negative sentiment than titles using decades-old procedural content generation, with players reading AI content as a sign of low developer investment. The authors argue successful adoption depends on deploying generative AI for what players actually need, not for what makes development cheaper.

title: Youth avoids Manchester cliches for city's first Cubitts eyewear store
blurb: Cubitts opened its first Manchester store, designed by local studio Youth to reference the city's industrial and musical history without leaning on the obvious visual cliches. Co-founders Oliver Collinge and Liam McGroarty built the interior around Manchester's present and future rather than heritage pastiche, a restrained approach to place-specific retail that most brand rollouts flatten into the same template.

title: RAGE-Vis:A Relation-Aware Generative Editing Interface for Natural Language-Based Chart Editing
blurb: RAGE-Vis is a research interface that turns bitmap chart images into an editable parameterized representation, then parses composite natural-language edits into targets and scopes rather than mapping each instruction to a single widget. The system flags fields affected by visual encoding, structural, and consistency relations and surfaces them as coordinated controls, so a request like reordering categories keeps legends and color mapping globally consistent.

title: New EU Guidelines For AI Labelling
blurb: The EU AI Act's transparency rules take effect August 2, 2026, requiring any company serving EU users to label deepfakes, chatbots, biometric tools, and unedited AI-written text on matters of public interest. The scope is narrower than the week's panic suggested: AI-assisted work reviewed by a named human editor is exempt, so most design and content workflows fall outside the disclosure mandate.

title: Zoom Annotation Flaws Could Let a Meeting Participant Hijack Another Attendee's Client
blurb: Three flaws in Zoom's annotation feature let any meeting participant achieve zero-interaction code execution on other attendees' clients, chaining a 128-byte stack buffer overflow with a missing sender-origin check that lets one malformed drawing reach every viewer. Zoom patched the bugs in June and July, roughly two months before public disclosure, with no exploitation reported and none of the three CVEs listed in CISA's KEV catalog.

title: Hackers Breach Polish Power Plant Controls via Private Cellular Network and Shut Turbine
blurb: Attackers shut down a steam turbine and process-water treatment system at a Polish combined heat and power plant serving 50,000 residents by pivoting from a compromised wind farm to a WAGO controller over the grid operator's private cellular APN, which CERT Polska calls the first observed real-world use of that vector. The controller ran default admin credentials and the APN permitted client-to-client traffic, so defenders should enable APN client isolation, treat the APN as untrusted from the OT side, and rotate default credentials.

title: Researchers Disclose AI-Assisted SharePoint Exploit Chain Reaching Unauthenticated RCE
blurb: Rapid7 disclosed CVE-2026-55040 (CVSS 9.1), a JWT-validation bypass in on-premises SharePoint that lets an unauthenticated attacker impersonate any user, then chained it to CVE-2026-63520 (CVSS 8.1), an unsafe .NET type instantiation in Business Connectivity Services, to reach unauthenticated RCE as the service account. Subscription Edition, 2019, and 2016 are affected; Rapid7 says the July update breaks the chain, so confirm it is installed and apply the pending August package.

title: Cisco pushes urgent patches for actively exploited zero-day flaw crashing firewalls
blurb: Cisco released urgent patches for an actively exploited zero-day in its firewall software that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker crash affected appliances, with no workarounds available. Admins running exposed Cisco firewalls should apply the fix immediately and treat internet-facing appliances as priority targets, since the flaw is being exploited in the wild for denial of service.

title: Researchers Turn USB Auto-Install Into a Full SYSTEM Takeover on Windows 11
blurb: Researchers demonstrated "Plug And Pwn," a technique that abuses Windows Plug and Play auto-install to reach SYSTEM on a fully updated Windows 11 machine, chaining an emulated Sierra Wireless service and a path-traversal flaw to plant a DLL in System32. An unprivileged user can trigger it locally via an emulated USB device or remotely over RDP when supported PnP and low-level USB redirection are enabled, which Microsoft says is off by default.

title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
blurb: Two malicious LiteLLM releases (versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8) sat on PyPI for about 40 minutes on March 24, harvesting cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords before quarantine, and CloudSEK's dataset now maps captured loot to 2,500+ organizations including NVIDIA, Cisco, and FedEx. Treat any install that day through 16:00 UTC as suspect and rotate all CI/CD secrets, publishing tokens, and cloud credentials rather than waiting for proof of misuse.

title: Cisco ASA and FTD Flaw Exploited in the Wild Can Trigger Remote DoS
blurb: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-20349 (CVSS 8.6), an insufficient-error-checking flaw in ASA and FTD software that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker crash the device via a crafted HTTP request to the Remote Access SSL VPN service, and it is already being exploited in the wild. Devices with SSL-VPN, IKEv2 Remote Access VPN client services, or Zero Trust Network Access enabled are affected, so patch to the fixed ASA and FTD hotfix builds immediately.

title: Microsoft Patches 398 Flaws Including a Windows Driver Zero-Day Under Active Attack
blurb: Microsoft's August update fixes 398 CVEs, including CVE-2026-68820 (CVSS 7.0), an actively exploited use-after-free in afd.sys that Check Point attributes to Lazarus and lets an attacker with local code execution escalate to SYSTEM. Patch the driver bug first despite its lower score, then queue the four unauthenticated RCEs rated CVSS 9.8 in Windows DNS Server, Deployment Services, QUIC, and HPC Pack.

title: Researchers Built a Fake Crypto Startup and Hired Three Suspected North Korean IT Workers
blurb: Security researchers built a fake DeFi protocol, Ballena Azul, advertised developer jobs, and hired three suspected North Korean IT workers onto recording-enabled work VMs to document the placement pipeline end to end. The onboarding paperwork is the reusable defensive signal: forged IDs with mismatched states, an image carrying a Google SynthID watermark and Gemini metadata, and a stolen license paired with a GPS-stripped iPhone 15 photo. Nobody exploited anything, because each operative cleared an interview, signed a contract, and received authorized access to source code and internal systems.

title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldBreak' zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges
blurb: Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse published "ShieldBreak," a Microsoft Defender zero-day that grants SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server 2025 systems where Defender is enabled. The exploit is a confirmed full bypass of RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656), which Microsoft patched in July, and no fix is yet available, so defenders should treat local privilege escalation on Defender-enabled hosts as unmitigated.

title: Attackers exploit critical SharePoint flaw after PoC goes public (CVE-2026-55040)
blurb: Threat actors have begun exploiting CVE-2026-55040, a critical authentication-bypass in Microsoft SharePoint, after Rapid7 published PoC code abusing flaws in the JWT token validation pipeline to impersonate site users or administrators. Microsoft patched the flaw in its July 2026 Patch Tuesday, and CISA urges admins to apply it, avoid exposing SharePoint to the internet, and front any exposed servers with an authenticating Layer 7 reverse proxy.

title: Microsoft-vendetta hacker has a new zero day that gives system privileges on fully patched Windows
blurb: A security researcher known for repeatedly targeting Microsoft disclosed a new zero-day local privilege escalation flaw that grants SYSTEM-level access on fully patched Windows, with no vendor fix currently available. The bug requires existing code execution to exploit, so treat it as a post-compromise escalation path and prioritize endpoint detection and least-privilege controls until Microsoft ships a patch.

title: Attackers Exploit SharePoint Authentication Bypass After Public PoC Release
blurb: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-55040 (CVSS 9.1), a critical SharePoint authentication bypass, using a Rapid7 PoC that chains four JWT validation flaws to forge tokens and impersonate any site user, including administrators, on unauthenticated servers. Microsoft patched the flaw in its July 2026 Patch Tuesday updates, and defenders should apply it immediately, as this is the fifth SharePoint vulnerability exploited in the wild this year.

title: Metabase SQL Zero-Day Attacks Could Have Wide Blast Radius
blurb: A maximum-severity SQL-injection zero-day (CVSS 10, no CVE yet) in Metabase versions 1.58 and above is under active exploitation, letting a remote attacker inject SQL into the application database and gain administrator access to steal stored database credentials, read connected data, and alter instance configuration. Metabase Cloud instances were auto-patched, but self-hosted deployments exposing the /api/session/reset_password endpoint (default API port 3000) remain vulnerable and should be patched and firewalled immediately.

title: Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access
blurb: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8), a directory-traversal flaw in Broadcom VMware vCenter that grants unauthenticated RCE, deploying a malicious cron job with reverse_ssh to establish persistent outbound access, per QUIRSO. Exploitation began August 3, five days after disclosure, and has hit 361 victim IPs across 47 countries, concentrated in Germany, the U.S., and Turkey. Patch immediately and hunt for unexpected reverse_ssh installs and outbound SSH.

title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code
blurb: SAP patched a maximum-severity flaw in Commerce Cloud's Data Hub Adapter (CVE-2026-58231, CVSS 10.0), where an unauthenticated attacker can abuse a default authentication client to submit crafted input to functions lacking validation, enabling arbitrary code execution. Apply the fixed Commerce Cloud release and re-deploy; as a temporary workaround, configure an IP Filter Set to restrict access to the vulnerable endpoint.

title: A Malicious SIM Card Can Run Attacker Code Inside the Modems Behind Cellular IoT Devices
blurb: Researchers at the University of Birmingham and Fuzzware showed that a hostile SIM card can issue RUN AT proactive commands to execute attacker code on the cellular modem inside IoT hardware, and demonstrated full takeover of a commercial EV charger. Nine of 26 tested devices accepted the command, mostly Quectel modules on a Qualcomm baseband; fleet operators should ask suppliers whether RUN AT is enabled in shipped firmware and can be disabled.

title: The LiteLLM supply chain attack this year could be the biggest ever
blurb: CloudSEK reports the March LiteLLM supply chain compromise exposed over 2,500 organizations, including Nvidia, Samsung, Cisco, ServiceNow, and Zscaler, after Team PCP pushed malicious PyPI releases that scraped cloud credentials, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and CI/CD secrets from /proc//mem across an estimated 434,000 pipelines. Treat any LLM API keys, gateway configs, and cloud credentials handled by affected pipelines as compromised and rotate them, since stolen valid credentials enable detection-evading logins rather than repeat intrusions.

title: Malicious SIMs can shut down phones, steal files, and drag 5G back to 2G
blurb: Malicious SIM cards can execute STK-based attacks that force phones to power off, exfiltrate stored files, and downgrade 5G connections to insecure 2G, exposing devices to interception and further exploitation. The technique abuses the SIM Application Toolkit's proactive commands, which handset baseband firmware trusts by default, so defenders should treat untrusted or unattended SIMs as a physical-access threat and restrict swaps in managed fleets.

title: Belgium's eID Authentication Opens Citizen Accounts to RCE
blurb: Vulnerabilities in Connective, a browser signing extension used for Belgian eID authentication across 60+ government agencies, 8 of the 10 largest banks, and 2M+ users, allowed attackers to steal identities and payment card data and achieve RCE on victims' machines. Disclosed by Bay Area Labs' James Arnott at DEF CON 34 and patched July 22, the flaws compromised the trust framework underlying the national ID system.

title: Hackers exploit critical Adobe Commerce flaw to hijack customer accounts
blurb: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-71362, a critical incorrect-authorization flaw in Adobe Commerce and Magento that lets an unauthenticated actor switch a customer session to another account and access private data, with no existing account or user interaction required. Adobe patched it yesterday alongside six other flaws and reports no in-the-wild exploitation, but Sansec says its WAF is already blocking active attempts, so treat exposed storefronts as targeted and patch immediately.

title: Critical 'Zoomsday' flaw enables total device takeover during Zoom calls — AI-assisted research only used 20 prompts to find an exploit to hack hundreds of millions of people.
blurb: Two RCE vulnerabilities in Zoom Workplace's always-on annotation library, dubbed "Zoomsday," let any meeting participant achieve invisible remote code execution on another attendee's device with no whiteboard interaction required. Zoom patched the bugs in versions 7.0.6 and 7.1.5 on the fast-track branch, so update immediately; researchers at A.Security built the working exploit against the fully proprietary client with just 20 prompts to an AI agent.

title: Coin-sized device can hack a Boeing 737’s Flight Management Computer, mess with takeoff weights, or even divert an aircraft — gadget connects to an easily accessible port that overrides commands from the pilots, uses in-flight Wi-Fi
blurb: Researchers from UC San Diego and Oberlin College built a coin-sized device that attaches to an unprotected diagnostic port in a Boeing 737's E&E bay, overriding signals between the MCDU and Flight Management Computer to alter takeoff weight data or navigation inputs. The attack requires physical access and hides under the port's dust cap, so operators should treat E&E bay access controls and avionics bus authentication as gaps to audit.

title: Prompt Injections for Defense
blurb: Researchers at Tracebit demonstrated "context bombing," a defensive technique that plants prompt injections alongside AWS-stored secrets like passwords and cryptographic keys to neutralize AI hacking agents. The injected prompts order the attacking LLM to perform guardrail-forbidden actions, such as detailing anthrax weaponization or referencing Tiananmen's Tank Man for Chinese models, causing it to shut down. The tactic only works against agents that carry guardrails, so defenders should expect diminishing returns as attackers shift to locally run models with no safety barriers.

title: Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws
blurb: Adobe patched three CVSS 10.0 flaws across ColdFusion (CVE-2026-48362, OS command injection), Campaign Classic (CVE-2026-71398 and CVE-2026-27302, both incorrect authorization), all enabling arbitrary code execution, alongside four other critical bugs in ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic. The ColdFusion and Campaign Classic updates carry a Priority 1 rating, and with no in-the-wild exploitation yet, administrators should patch on-premise deployments within 72 hours.

title: DeadLock Ransomware Uses Polygon Smart Contracts to Make Extortion Infra Harder to Disrupt
blurb: DeadLock ransomware now anchors its extortion infrastructure to Polygon smart contracts and the Session messaging network, storing and delivering leak resources on-chain to resist takedowns, per Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The group has claimed 96 victims since July 2025, encrypts with Curve25519 and XChaCha20 to a ".dlock" extension, and is being deployed by multiple actors, including a Lynx and INC affiliate.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.6-Cyber with Reduced Safeguards for Exploit Development
blurb: OpenAI released GPT-5.6-Cyber through a new Daybreak Red tier, a model tuned for exploit-chain development, authentication bypass, and privilege escalation with refusals deliberately reduced. Its internal Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate hits 95%, versus 1.5% for the general GPT-5.6 Sol. The model already surfaced CVE-2026-15903 (CVSS 8.8), a V8 out-of-bounds read/write, so defenders should expect faster weaponization of novel bugs and prioritize patch velocity accordingly.

title: Mozilla revokes Firefox signing key after unencrypted copy lands in GitHub
blurb: Mozilla revoked a Firefox add-on signing key after an unencrypted copy was committed to a public GitHub repository, exposing it to anyone who could clone the repo. The key could have been used to sign malicious extensions that Firefox would trust, so operators should force add-on updates and verify installed extensions against Mozilla's reissued signing chain.

title: Spaghettifying DRAM
blurb: skitter-creek-bath-salts manipulates the AMD DRAM controller's address-translation registers to remap physical memory and expose protected carveouts invisible to the kernel, unlocking the Platform Security Processor, System Management Mode, C6 DRAM, and CPU microcode. The technique was developed on AMD Family 16h parts, the last generation whose datasheets document the translation registers and confirm they cannot be locked, with 17h and later omitting the details rather than fixing the exposure.

title: WordPress 7.0.4 Patches Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
blurb: WordPress released version 7.0.4 to patch CVE-2026-65640 (CVSS 8.8), an authenticated RCE that lets Author-level users upload a PNG containing embedded PostScript, which ImageMagick passes to Ghostscript for execution. Only installations using Imagick and Ghostscript are affected; the fix is backported to all branches down to 4.7, and multi-author or open-registration sites should patch immediately given the low privilege bar.

title: Critical VMware vCenter Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
blurb: An APT actor is actively exploiting CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8), a directory-traversal-to-RCE flaw in VMware vCenter's Syslog server that lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access run arbitrary code, patched by Broadcom on July 29. Quirso tracked exploitation starting August 3 across 360-plus victim IPs in 47 countries, with attackers dropping the reverse_ssh framework for persistent outbound access, so patch edge-exposed vCenter and hunt for unexpected outbound connections.

title: When Agents Talk: Honeytokens under Shared Memory
blurb: This paper argues that honeytokens cannot stay invisible to trusted AI agents while remaining undetectable to an attacker who shares their information, because any trusted rule that avoids decoys can be copied, and shared memory lets a coalition pool weak fingerprints to drive Bayes classification error toward zero. The authors' fix is to keep token identity in a private reference monitor and route legitimate agents through a provenance-enforcing broker. Honeytokens remain useful sensors, but they need a separate security boundary.

title: Shattering the Dream - When a Job Offer Becomes a Zero-Day Attack
blurb: A wave of the Operation Dream Job campaign is targeting defense, aerospace, and aviation firms worldwide with trojanized PDF viewers that deploy a new FudModule rootkit, which exploits a Windows AFD.sys local privilege escalation zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) to gain SYSTEM and blind EDR. Microsoft patched the flaw on August 11 in its August Patch Tuesday updates, so prioritize deployment and hunt for RelayShell webshells on compromised Roundcube and WordPress infrastructure.

title: Terabytes of credentials leaked in massive supply-chain attack
blurb: A supply-chain compromise of LiteLLM, the open-source AI development tool, exposed terabytes of credentials from over 2,500 organizations including Microsoft, Amazon, Cisco, Samsung, and Salesforce, per CloudSEK and Hudson Rock. Attackers pulled cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets, and package-publishing tokens during a 40-minute window in March from trojanized PyPI builds, so any org that installed LiteLLM in that period should rotate all affected secrets immediately.

title: Sandworm-Linked UAC-0145 Uses Fake Job Interviews to Push VPN That Can Run Commands
blurb: CERT-UA disclosed an ongoing campaign by UAC-0145, a Sandworm (APT44/GRU) subgroup, that lures Ukrainian sysadmins and IT specialists with fake recruiter outreach and Zoom interviews, then delivers a trojanized VPN client called SopraVPN capable of executing arbitrary commands. Victims are steered to SourceForge-hosted projects spoofing Sopra Steria Bulgaria after bogus WireGuard configs fail; defenders should block the soprasteria-bg[.]com lookalike domain and flag IT-recruitment lures shifting to Telegram.

title: Malicious MCP Servers Can Split Instructions to Make AI Coding Agents Exfiltrate Secrets
blurb: Researchers at ASSET Research Group disclosed GhostSplice, a technique where a malicious MCP server splits an exfiltration request across a tool description and a tool result so no single fragment looks harmful, letting an AI coding agent stitch them together to leak SSH keys, .env secrets, and source code. Splitting the request into two channels raised average agent compliance from 42% to 82% and bypassed refusals that blocked the unsplit version.

title: Adobe Commerce Bug Targeted Immediately After Disclosure
blurb: Attackers began exploiting a critical Adobe Commerce authorization flaw (CVE-2026-71362, CVSS 9.1) within hours of disclosure, letting unauthenticated attackers hijack customer sessions and take over accounts, per Sansec. Adobe patched it on August 2026 Patch Tuesday across all Commerce, Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source builds through the July 2026 release; apply the isolated patch immediately and treat exposed storefronts as targeted.

title: Locking your ssh-agent exposed local-only keys until OpenSSH 10.5
blurb: OpenSSH 10.5 patches a flaw introduced in 10.4 where locking your ssh-agent silently disabled the session-bind check that distinguishes local requests from forwarded ones, letting operations meant to be local-only, such as adding PKCS#11 tokens and using destination-restricted keys, run over a forwarded connection. The release also fixes a use-after-free in the ssh client and a "restrict" keyword in authorized_keys that failed to disable tunnel forwarding.

title: ShieldBreak Zero-Day PoC Claims Microsoft Defender Patch Bypass With SYSTEM Access
blurb: A researcher going by Chaotic Eclipse released a proof-of-concept for ShieldBreak, a full patch bypass for CVE-2026-50656 (CVSS 7.8, aka RoguePlanet), a race condition in Microsoft Defender's mpengine.dll that spawns a SYSTEM-level shell. The PoC claims a 100% success rate on fully patched Windows 11 25H2 and Windows Server 2025, with Windows 10 also affected but unsupported by the exploit.

title: BdThemes Supply Chain Attack Poisons JSON to Create Rogue WordPress Admins
blurb: Attackers compromised the Sigmative API feeding BdThemes' Biggopti promotional-banner component, poisoning a static JSON stream to exploit an XSS flaw (CVSS 5.4) in its "display_id" parsing and silently create rogue admin accounts on every wp-admin page load. No WordPress.org source was modified, so defenders running the seven affected Elementor plugins, including Element Pack (100,000+ installs), should audit admin users and remove the plugins pending WordPress.org's full review.

title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops Windows Zero-Day Exploit ‘ShieldBreak’
blurb: Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse published ShieldBreak, a proof-of-concept exploit that abuses Microsoft Defender's cloud-hydration scan via the Cloud Filter API to plant a malicious phoneinfo.dll in System32 and spawn a SYSTEM shell on fully patched Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025. Defender must be active for the exploit to run, so defenders should deploy Kevin Beaumont's published detection queries and watch for QueueReporting task abuse until Microsoft ships a fix.

title: Android malware combo takes out loans and relays victims' credit cards
blurb: Group-IB documented a fraud chain pairing the SpyNote RAT with a new NFC relay tool, WindRelay, that let attackers take out a bank loan and cash out a victim's card in a single 13-minute vishing call. After social-engineering the victim into sideloading SpyNote and granting Accessibility permissions, the attacker silently installed WindRelay, which relayed live NFC transaction data and the victim-supplied PIN to a terminal-side device for fraudulent purchases.

title: "City-Forum" data-theft attacks target Salesforce, ServiceNow portals
blurb: An ongoing campaign dubbed City-Forum, tracked by Reco, is exfiltrating data from misconfigured Salesforce Experience Cloud and ServiceNow customer portals by abusing overly permissive guest-user access rather than any product vulnerability. All activity traces to a single Contabo-hosted IP (158.220.87.79) using the default Go-http-client user agent, enumerating Salesforce Aura objects via HostConfigController and SelectableListDataProviderController, so defenders should audit guest-account sharing rules and lock down anonymous portal permissions now.

title: An Empirical Study of Output-to-Input Loops for Black-Box Backdoor Detection in Fine-Tuned Open-Weight LLMs
blurb: This paper introduces self-feeding, a black-box method for detecting backdoors in downloaded fine-tuned LLMs by feeding a model's own output back as its next input until the text drifts toward its fine-tuning data and trips a hidden trigger. Across six open-weight models and eleven attack categories, it flagged five at 92% pooled precision, versus one of 120 prompt-model pairs for a same-prompt baseline. Four-step chains hold 100% model-level precision while cutting queries 60%.

title: AWS key exposed in JavaScript may have lit way to Beacon's charity data
blurb: Researchers found an AWS access key hardcoded in client-side JavaScript served by charity CRM provider Beacon, potentially exposing the personal and donor data of the nonprofits using the platform. Any visitor could extract the key from the page source, so affected organizations should assume the credential was harvested, rotate the AWS key immediately, and audit CloudTrail for unauthorized S3 or database access.

title: Kimwolf botnet rebuilt to survive takedowns, researchers say
blurb: Palo Alto Unit 42 reported a new version of the Kimwolf/Aisuru botnet, active since February and largely powered by hijacked Android TV boxes, that adds an HTTP/2 flood mimicking full Chrome browser fingerprints to evade traffic-filtering defenses. It also resolves its C2 address via Ethereum Name Service, with five rotating providers and a Tor hidden-service fallback, leaving no registrar or domain record for law enforcement to seize.

title: Spectre rears its ugly head again as researchers show some RISC-V chips are susceptible
blurb: Researchers demonstrated that some RISC-V processors remain vulnerable to Spectre-style speculative-execution attacks, allowing an attacker to leak data across security boundaries by mistraining branch prediction and reading secrets through cache side channels. The finding extends a class of microarchitectural flaws first disclosed in 2018 to RISC-V silicon, so affected vendors will need firmware or hardware mitigations while operators weigh the performance cost of disabling speculation on exposed workloads.

title: In a first, US will allow some private firms to carry out cyberattacks
blurb: The Trump administration published a presidential memorandum authorizing vetted private companies to conduct offensive cyber operations, including spyware surveillance and disruptive attacks that destroy data or systems, against foreign criminal gangs and hackers. Participating firms must deposit $1M in escrow and secure sign-offs from the DOJ and DHS per operation, with government guidance on eligibility due within two months and legal challenges expected.

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report H1 2026: 1 Tbps attacks soar as DNS floods and geopolitical tensions drive a new wave
blurb: Cloudflare mitigated 935 network-layer DDoS attacks exceeding 1 Tbps in H1 2026, a 519% quarter-over-quarter jump, as the attack mix shifted from botnet floods toward DNS-based reflection and amplification. DNS Floods climbed from 25.7% to 40.0% of network-layer activity and CLDAP Floods surged 580% to become the #3 vector, so defenders should prioritize UDP reflection filtering and DNS-layer rate limiting over botnet-focused controls.

title: Trump turns to private sector in offensive hacking operations memo
blurb: Trump signed a national security memorandum directing a federal coordination center to authorize vetted private companies to run cyber surveillance and cyber effects operations against foreign transnational criminal organizations, under DOJ or DHS contracts and federal oversight. The program must operate within existing law, including the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, though critics warn that outsourcing offensive operations to the private sector risks weak accountability and scope creep.

title: 153GB of stolen credentials surface after LiteLLM supply chain attack
blurb: A 153GB archive stolen in the LiteLLM supply chain attack has surfaced, exposing 118,829 CI runner dumps and millions of secrets tied to 2,488 corporate domains including AWS, Cisco, Salesforce, Microsoft, and NVIDIA. TeamPCP poisoned Trivy to steal LiteLLM's PyPI tokens, then published malicious versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on March 24, so teams that installed those releases should rotate all pipeline credentials and revoke exposed provider API keys immediately.

title: The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark
blurb: SRE-Bench is the first contamination-free reverse-engineering benchmark for AI agents, built from scratch by RE experts over 5,000 hours across 19 private real-world-scale programs, 262 binary instances, and 1,572 deterministically graded tasks. Across five frontier models, RE remains largely unsolved: the strongest, GPT-5.6-sol, scores 61.4% per instance and fully solves only 31.5%. The authors find strong source-code security skills do not transfer to binary analysis, and that agents are oddly insensitive to compiler optimization and static linking.

title: OpenSSH 10.5/10.5p1
blurb: OpenSSH 10.5 fixes a ssh-agent flaw where agent locking failed to block session-bind requests, letting a remote attacker add PKCS#11 tokens and use keys carrying destination restrictions that were meant for local-only use. The team also announced a shift to more frequent releases, citing AI-assisted bug reports that adversaries could independently rediscover, and portable builds now require ECC support including NISTP521 in libcrypto.

title: Fortinet Patches Authentication Flaws in FortiWeb and FortiManager
blurb: Fortinet patched eight vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-26035, an improper-authentication flaw in FortiWeb that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker log into the GUI/CLI with any username and password when the non-default wildcard admin setting is enabled. Patch to FortiWeb 8.0.3, 7.6.7, 7.4.12, or 7.2.13, or disable the wildcard setting as a workaround; no exploitation has been reported.

title: AI for Military Support
blurb: A study of 2,015 Israeli military personnel testing a replica AI targeting decision-support system found algorithmic aversion rather than automation bias, with operators most likely to reject algorithmic recommendations in high-collateral-damage scenarios. Adding explainable-AI features to the interface reduced that aversion and increased trust, suggesting interface design, not just model accuracy, shapes how human operators weigh AI targeting recommendations.

title: Plaintext Recovery Against Post-Filtering Access Control
blurb: This paper introduces reconstruction attacks against fine-grained access control systems that rely on post-filtering, where untrusted queries run over all data before private results are redacted. Using rich predicates like range, prefix, and conjunctive queries, the authors amplify existence leakage into full-record recovery via a PostgreSQL RLS timing side-channel and term recovery from an Elasticsearch/OpenSearch DLS scoring side-channel.

title: Gunra Ransomware Gang Exploits Fortinet Flaws, Bypasses MFA
blurb: Gunra, a Conti-derived ransomware-as-a-service operation, is exploiting two known Fortinet authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-55591, CVSS 9.8, and CVE-2025-24472) for initial access against critical infrastructure and government targets, per a joint FBI and South Korean advisory. Both are on CISA's KEV catalog and grant super-admin privileges on unpatched FortiOS and FortiProxy appliances, so treat internet-facing Fortinet devices as compromised and patch immediately.

title: Cisco fixes vulnerability exploited to DoS its firewalls (CVE-2026-20349)
blurb: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-20349, a high-severity flaw in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of ASA and FTD software that lets unauthenticated attackers send a crafted HTTP request to reload appliances into a denial-of-service state. It's in CISA's KEV catalog with a federal remediation deadline of August 14; apply Cisco's hot fixes, as there are no workarounds.

title: AI Guardrail Survival under Single-Cycle Agentic Self-Summarization
blurb: This paper shows that when long-running agents compact their context via self-summarization, safety rules can survive as text but stop functioning, so auditing for a rule's presence is not the same as verifying it still fires. Behavioral replay found degraded rule residues drove prohibited actions 34 to 57 points more often than intact rules, and the failure is silent at runtime. Defenders should validate constraints against an external registry and test enforcement behaviorally rather than trusting LLM-judge or presence-based checks.

title: Chinese Loongson processors have leaky caches, researchers find
blurb: Researchers disclosed that Chinese Loongson processors leak data through their cache subsystem, enabling a side-channel attack that lets one process infer memory contents belonging to another. Organizations running Loongson-based hardware, common in Chinese government and domestic deployments, should treat the affected chips as vulnerable to cross-process data exposure and prioritize microarchitectural mitigations or workload isolation until a firmware fix ships.

title: 421 bugs in Microsoft's Patch Tuesday release, and the Norks have already attacked one
blurb: Microsoft's August Patch Tuesday fixed 421 vulnerabilities, one of them a zero-day already exploited in the wild by North Korean state actors. Administrators should prioritize the actively exploited flaw for immediate patching and treat exposed systems as potential compromise, then work through the remaining critical-rated bugs across the release before the exploit pool widens.

title: White House taps security firms for offensive hack-back operations
blurb: A White House memorandum signed by President Trump directs the National Coordination Center to build a program letting vetted private security firms apply for U.S.-authorized offensive operations against foreign cybercrime organizations. Participating companies must post at least $1M in bond or escrow, forfeit it for noncompliance, and halt operations immediately if they hit U.S. citizens or systems.

title: OpenAI has paused work on its Astra AI model after it passed a 'critical threshold' in cyber capability – but it’s not the one that breached Hugging Face
blurb: OpenAI paused internal work on its next-gen Astra model after evaluations found it crossed the "Critical" cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework, meaning it can develop functional zero-day exploits across severity levels and run end-to-end attacks on hardened targets without human intervention. It's the first model OpenAI has self-rated Critical rather than High. The company added chain-of-thought monitoring for misalignment and tightened external access controls, but clarified Astra was not the model that breached Hugging Face last month.

title: Deeply buried 16-year-old SQLite bug caused last year's Tailscale outages
blurb: A 16-year-old bug in SQLite, involving mishandled index optimization during query planning, was identified as the root cause of the Tailscale outages that disrupted service last year. Tailscale traced the intermittent failures to the deeply buried defect after extended debugging, and the fix has since landed upstream in SQLite, closing a fault that had gone unnoticed across the database's widely deployed codebase.

title: Mystery attacker spent a year raiding Salesforce and ServiceNow portals
blurb: An unidentified threat actor spent roughly a year systematically raiding customer-facing Salesforce and ServiceNow portals, exfiltrating data by abusing legitimate portal access rather than exploiting a single flaw. Defenders should audit SaaS portal permissions and guest-user access, review anomalous export and query volumes over the past 12 months, and tighten object-level access controls that these platforms leave permissive by default.

title: Long-running Data Theft Campaign Targeting Salesforce, ServiceNow
blurb: An unknown threat actor has run the "City-Forum" campaign since at least March 2025, using custom tooling to steal data from Salesforce and ServiceNow instances with over-permissioned guest access across telecom, finance, and public-sector targets. Researchers at Reco note the actor reached undocumented interfaces like Salesforce's LWR data-access layer and an obscure ServiceNow Service Portal search endpoint, so defenders should audit and lock down guest-accessible surfaces.

title: Backdoor Decontamination Dynamics in LLM Agents
blurb: This paper studies whether "defensive poisoning" can scrub unknown backdoors from open-weight, tool-calling LLM agents: install a known trigger, then unlearn it and hope the hidden one clears as a side effect. Across 115 experiments on AgentDyn, defensive poisoning alone erased about 56% of original backdoors, and follow-up decontamination drove nearly all survivors to erasure, including 87% of co-resident backdoors. J-lens probing showed benign outputs restored but traces of the original trigger awareness persisting in intermediate layers.

title: Delta investigates in-flight Wi-Fi spoofing on post-DEF CON flight from Las Vegas
blurb: Delta is investigating an evil-twin attack on flight 591 from Las Vegas to Atlanta, where a passenger allegedly ran a rogue access point named "Delta WiFi Fast" to phish fellow travelers, prompting the crew to disable in-flight Wi-Fi for 30 minutes and law enforcement to board on arrival. ACARS messages flagged the passenger as trying to scam others; Delta says flight safety and aircraft systems were unaffected and that it is coordinating with the FBI and FAA.

title: A month with Anthropic’s Mythos left Rubrik rethinking remediation
blurb: Rubrik spent a month running Anthropic's Mythos Preview model against its own codebase and rebuilt its review pipeline around the findings rather than hiring reviewers. CTO Arvind Nithrakashyap said the work went into the harness wrapping the model, encoding trust boundaries and business context rather than prompts, with wide repository scans narrowing over successive passes. Rubrik limits machine remediation to vulnerability classes it judges reliable and well-scoped, routing everything else to an engineer with a structured plan, choosing trustworthy automation over maximum automation.

title: Kimwolf v7 Android Botnet Makes HTTP/2 DDoS Traffic Look Like Legitimate Browsing
blurb: Unit 42 discovered Kimwolf v7, an Android and IoT botnet variant that adds an nghttp2-powered HTTP/2 flood constructing complete browser fingerprints to make DDoS traffic indistinguishable from legitimate browsing at the protocol and header level. The update also hardens C2 against takedown using tiered ENS resolution, a hard-coded Tor .onion fallback, and a local proxy, so defenders should lock down Android TV boxes exposing ADB on port 5555.

title: Mozilla Revokes Firefox and Thunderbird Linux Signing Key After Key Lands in Private Repo
blurb: Mozilla revoked the OpenPGP subkey used to sign Firefox and Thunderbird Linux downloads after an unencrypted copy was accidentally committed to a private company repository, publishing a replacement subkey (fingerprint ending 7676 7AA3) valid through August 2028. The revocation certificate uses reason code 2 ("key material has been compromised"), so signatures from the old key stop verifying once users import it, breaking verification of older tarballs and RPM updates for anyone who checks signatures by hand.

title: Two wars and a World Cup lead to epic DDoS attacks on publishers
blurb: Two active wars and the run-up to the World Cup have driven a surge of record-scale DDoS attacks against news publishers, according to The Register's reporting on the latest mitigation data. Media and publishing sites should assume they are high-value targets during major geopolitical and sporting events, and confirm upstream DDoS scrubbing and rate-limiting are provisioned to absorb hyper-volumetric floods before the next spike.

title: Feds warn Gunra ransomware is exploiting known bugs to hit critical infrastructure
blurb: US agencies warned that the Gunra ransomware crew is chaining known, already-patched vulnerabilities to breach and encrypt critical-infrastructure networks rather than relying on novel zero-days. Defenders should prioritize patching anything on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on internet-facing assets, since the campaign's entry vector is unpatched edge systems rather than a new flaw requiring detection engineering.

title: Cyberattack on logistics giant CEVA delivers customer data into the wrong hands
blurb: CEVA Logistics, the France-based freight and supply-chain operator, disclosed a cyberattack that exposed customer data to unauthorized parties. Organizations that share shipment manifests, contact records, or account details with CEVA should assume that data is now in criminal hands and monitor for targeted phishing and business-email-compromise attempts referencing legitimate logistics activity.

title: PQC in Plaintext: Google Cloud’s post-quantum cryptography roadmap
blurb: Google Cloud published a roadmap to migrate its internal infrastructure and customer-facing services to post-quantum cryptography by 2029, ahead of CNSA 2.0 and the NIST IR 8547 deprecation window of 2030-2035. The strategy prioritizes Store Now, Decrypt Later mitigation, signature integrity against forgery, and cryptographic agility, with PQC extending to Sovereign Cloud offerings (GCD, GDC) and AI workloads. Defenders holding long-lived secrets should treat SNDL harvesting as an active threat and begin inventorying quantum-vulnerable key exchanges now.

title: Trezor shipping provider breach exposes personal data of nearly 14,000 customers
blurb: A breach at Trezor's shipping provider ShipMonk exposed the names, email addresses, phone numbers, and home addresses of roughly 13,700 hardware wallet customers across the US, UK, and five other countries. Trezor's internal systems and the wallets remain secure, but exposed customers should treat unsolicited contact impersonating Trezor, banks, or exchanges as phishing and never disclose their seed phrases.

title: Microsoft threatened legal action, and this researcher just dropped a new Windows bug anyway
blurb: Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse published ShieldBreak, an unpatched Windows Defender local privilege escalation that elevates a low-privileged user to SYSTEM on Windows 10, 11, and Server 2025, with a working proof-of-concept confirmed by Will Dormann. The exploit requires Defender enabled and the victim to run a supplied app, and bypasses Microsoft's earlier fix for the related RoguePlanet bug; Microsoft is investigating and no patch exists yet.

title: Delta Airlines flight Wi-Fi tampered with after DEF CON conference
blurb: A passenger on a Las Vegas-to-Atlanta Delta flight broadcast a rogue "Delta WiFi Fast" access point on Monday, apparently using a Wi-Fi Pineapple to run deauthentication attacks and serve a phishing page that harvested passenger credentials and Google logins. Crew flagged the fake network via ACARS messages to ground staff, and federal authorities boarded at the gate to detain the suspect and seize the broadcasting hardware.

title: White House Mobilizes Security Firms for Operations Against Foreign Cybercrime Gangs
blurb: A White House memorandum issued Wednesday establishes a National Coordination Center program authorizing vetted private US firms to run offensive and intelligence-gathering cyber operations against foreign cyber-enabled criminal organizations under federal control. Participating companies must sign DOJ or DHS contracts backed by a bond or escrow of at least $1M, obtain written executive-director approval per operation, and stay within limits barring lethal effects or strikes on US persons.

title: Chrome adopts what may be the best protection yet against account takeovers
blurb: Chrome now generates device-bound session credentials (DBSCs) on recent Windows and macOS builds, binding session cookies to a TPM- or secure-enclave-resident key that never leaves the device. This neutralizes cookie theft from infostealers and adversary-in-the-middle attacks, since a cookie exfiltrated to an attacker's browser is useless without the hardware-backed key, closing a gap that phishing-resistant MFA and passkeys left open.

title: 'Jewelbug' APT Balances State Espionage & Cryptocurrency Theft
blurb: Symantec attributes "Jewelbug," a China-based hacker-for-hire APT, to a single custom C2 panel that runs state-aligned espionage against government, military, and telecom targets in Asia and the Middle East alongside large-scale cryptocurrency theft. Its toolset includes the Antino Windows backdoor, ClientKing Linux backdoor, and a "PDF Viewer" browser extension that steals cookies, session tokens, and can silently swap crypto wallet addresses mid-transaction.

title: Zoom flaw let an attacker take over your device, including iPhone and Mac
blurb: Researchers at A Security disclosed a Zoom vulnerability that allowed silent, zero-interaction remote code execution against any participant on a screen-sharing call, affecting Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. Zoom has patched the flaw; notably, the team found it in early June using publicly available AI models in fewer than 20 prompts, work they estimate previously would have taken five people six months.

title: Extension Banned for Stealing AI Chats Returns to Chrome Store, Resumes Malicious Activities
blurb: A Chrome extension ('AI Sidebar with DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Claude and more') that Google pulled in January 2026 for scraping ChatGPT and DeepSeek conversations is back on the Web Store and reaching enterprise endpoints via Google's CDN, per Netskope.
