blurb: Google added two usability features to Connected Sheets: list parameters that let queries reference a grid range of cell values as multiple filter inputs, and column aliasing that swaps unwieldy BigQuery column names for presentation-ready labels without changing the underlying reference. Both let business users self-serve BigQuery analysis through drop-downs and readable labels instead of editing queries, and are rolling out to all Workspace customers and personal accounts.

title: Improved file importing in Google Sheets with tables and linked pivot tables
blurb: Google Sheets now imports Excel tables as native Sheets tables and fully supports Excel pivot tables backed by table ranges, preserving formatting and linked data on conversion. The change removes the manual reconstruction Workspace users previously faced when migrating Excel files, and it rolls out to all Workspace customers and personal accounts with no admin control, starting August 11 with pivot table support reaching full visibility within 15 days.

title: Ransomware gangs skip the CEO, head straight for the 40-something IT manager
blurb: Ransomware crews increasingly target mid-level IT managers, not executives, since those admins hold the credentials and access that unlock networks.

title: What vibe-coding startup valuations portend for CIOs
blurb: The author argues that soaring vibe-coding valuations, led by Lovable's $13.3B Series C, signal VCs betting these tools become a standing CIO line item rather than a developer niche. Unlike Cursor and Windsurf, which target engineers, Lovable and Replit ($9B) aim at business users, following the no-code path into the enterprise through chat-driven app prototyping. For CIOs, the shift moves app-building beyond IT, raising governance and shadow-IT questions as CEOs and customer-success staff ship working prototypes in hours.

title: Corporate conversations about AI productivity mostly focus on future gains
blurb: A new report from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis found that most corporate AI-productivity discussions on earnings calls center on expected future gains rather than results already booked. The framing signals that enterprise AI spending remains largely a bet, leaving CIOs to justify current infrastructure and licensing costs against returns that vendors and executives concede are still quarters away.

title: AWS wants to lower cloud compute crunch with Kubernetes updates
blurb: AWS added a cluster-wide control-plane configuration to Amazon EKS, letting customers tune four Kubernetes API server, scheduler, and controller-manager parameters covering pod placement, autoscaling responsiveness, event retention, and NodePort allocation without running bespoke components. The bin-packing scheduler option concentrates pods onto fewer nodes to cut idle capacity and compute costs, which removes the operational overhead teams running high-churn AI, batch, and CI/CD workloads previously carried.

title: AI hyperscale and agentic demands helped Cisco smash revenue records
blurb: Cisco closed fiscal 2026 with record revenue of $63.3B, up 12% YoY, as AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers hit $9.3B for the year, roughly 4.5 times the FY2025 total. Q4 revenue rose 18% to $17.3B on 24% product growth, with Silicon One systems and coherent optics driving hyperscale demand for the scale-across networking that links distributed AI data centers.

title: Rent-a-GPU outfit Nebius promises rapid 1 GW powerup plan isn't nebulous
blurb: Nebius committed to bringing 1 GW of GPU capacity online rapidly, funding the buildout through aggressive debt and equity financing to keep pace with rivals like CoreWeave. The plan gives enterprise buyers another neocloud option for renting Nvidia capacity, but the leverage-heavy approach raises the same margin-durability questions dogging every AI infrastructure operator scaling this fast.

title: Twitch feeds your streams to Amazon's AI unless you tell it to stop
blurb: Twitch now feeds user streams into Amazon's AI training by default, requiring an explicit opt-out to stop it.

title: FCC bolsters IoT cybersecurity with security trust mark push
blurb: The FCC opened its filing window for Cybersecurity Label Administrators under the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark program, granting conditional approval to IIA Lab Services and Element Materials Technology as it stands up a voluntary security-labeling scheme for consumer IoT products. CLAs automatically lose authority if they become affiliated with any vendor on the FCC's Covered List, which now spans foreign-made routers and firms tied to Chinese telecoms, tying the certification directly to supply-chain vetting.

title: Zoom Patches "Zoomsday" Zero-Click Flaw Enabling Remote Code Execution
blurb: Zoom patched CVE-2026-53413, a zero-click memory-corruption flaw dubbed "Zoomsday" in its annotation feature that let any meeting participant execute code on another attendee's device across Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, and Linux clients through version 7.0.5. IT teams should push the updated clients immediately, since a single crafted message in a large meeting could compromise many participants at once and enable data theft, camera access, or malware installation.

title: Hackers Breach Polish Power Plant Controls via Private Cellular Network and Shut Turbine
blurb: CERT Polska disclosed that attackers shut down a steam turbine and process-water treatment at a Polish combined heat and power plant by pivoting from a compromised wind farm through a shared private cellular APN, the first real-world use of that vector. The APN allowed client-to-client traffic and the reachable WAGO controller still had default credentials, so CERT's fix is APN client isolation and treating cellular links as untrusted from the OT side.

title: A practical guide to solving when zero+zero=two in mesh observability
blurb: This CNCF post explains why distributed traces break when you layer a service mesh (Istio/Kiali) on top of application-level OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and how to reconnect them so mesh and app spans land in the same transaction. The fix hinges on consistent context propagation and an OpenTelemetry Collector that ingests telemetry from both the mesh and the app in different formats. Metrics and logs survive the mismatch, but traces are the piece that silently falls apart until you wire the Collector correctly.

title: A Malicious SIM Card Can Run Attacker Code Inside the Modems Behind Cellular IoT Devices
blurb: Researchers at the University of Birmingham and Fuzzware showed that a malicious SIM can issue a proactive RUN AT command to execute attacker code on the cellular modem, and they used it to take over a commercial EV charger. The flaw hit 9 of 26 tested devices, mostly Quectel machine-to-machine modules in EV chargers, industrial routers, and telematics units, so operators should ask suppliers whether RUN AT is enabled and can be disabled.

title: Cisco pushes urgent patches for actively exploited zero-day flaw crashing firewalls
blurb: Cisco issued emergency patches for a zero-day in its firewall software that lets unauthenticated attackers crash devices remotely, with active exploitation already underway and no workarounds available. SREs running Cisco firewalls should treat this as a same-day patch given the DoS blast radius and the lack of any mitigation short of updating the affected appliances.

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report H1 2026: 1 Tbps attacks soar as DNS floods and geopolitical tensions drive a new wave
blurb: Cloudflare mitigated 935 network-layer DDoS attacks exceeding 1 Tbps in the first half of 2026, a 519% quarter-over-quarter jump, as DNS floods climbed to 40% of network-layer activity and CLDAP reflection surged 580% to become the #3 vector. Media and government were the hardest-hit sectors amid coverage of Iran, Ukraine, and the World Cup, with H1 volume averaging roughly 5,300 mitigated attacks per hour.

title: OpenSSH 10.5/10.5p1
blurb: OpenSSH 10.5 patches an ssh-agent flaw where agent locking broke the session-bind extension, letting operations meant to be local-only run remotely, including adding PKCS#11 tokens and using keys with destination restrictions. The team is now shipping more frequent point releases to get fixes out faster, citing a rise in AI-assisted bug reports, and Portable builds now require ECC support in libcrypto.

title: PQC in Plaintext: Google Cloud’s post-quantum cryptography roadmap
blurb: Google Cloud published its post-quantum cryptography roadmap, committing to full PQC readiness across internal infrastructure and customer-facing services by 2029, ahead of the CNSA 2.0 and NIST IR 8547 deprecation windows of 2030-2035. The strategy prioritizes Store Now, Decrypt Later mitigation, signature integrity, and cryptographic agility, with rollouts extending to Sovereign Cloud offerings like Google Distributed Cloud and to AI workloads.

title: We’re open-sourcing our privacy proxy CLI
blurb: Cloudflare open-sourced pvcli, a command-line tool for debugging privacy-preserving protocols like Oblivious HTTP, which spread work across relay, gateway, and origin parties and are hard to trace when requests fail. Released under Apache-2.0, it executes a full OHTTP request in a single command, drawing on Cloudflare's experience running Privacy Proxy and Gateway at millions of requests per second for Apple Private Relay and Microsoft Edge Secure Network.

title: Advancing AI model interoperability with Docker and ModelPack
blurb: The ModelPack project partnered with Docker to standardize how AI models are packaged and distributed, using OCI artifacts to decouple models from the specific tool or framework that produced them. The collaboration integrates Docker's Model Runner with ModelPack's open format, letting platform teams push, store, and pull models through the same OCI registries they already run for container images.

title: CNCF Announces Graduation of Cloud Native Buildpacks, Advancing the Standard for Container Builds
blurb: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation graduated Cloud Native Buildpacks, its toolkit for building OCI-compliant container images directly from source code by automating language detection, dependency installation, and image layering. The roadmap targets expanded OCI Artifacts support, stronger SBOM workflows, and WebAssembly compatibility, with Bloomberg and Heroku by Salesforce among the active code contributors.

title: Canva redesigns session revocation for 100M active sessions
blurb: Canva rebuilt its session revocation system to handle hundreds of millions of active sessions without a networked database lookup on most auth requests. Instead of hitting MySQL, gateways read 16-byte binary revocation records from immutable 30-minute S3 objects, using conditional GETs to pull only changed chunks and sorted in-memory arrays that cut the revocation cache footprint by 87.5%. The writeup treats S3 as a coordination primitive, with conditional PUTs for optimistic concurrency and ZooKeeper leader election as an optional conflict-reducer rather than a correctness requirement.

title: Accelerate PostgreSQL migrations using Gemini in Database Migration Service
blurb: Google added AI-assisted code conversion powered by Gemini to Database Migration Service, targeting the stored procedures, triggers, and custom functions that stall Oracle and SQL Server migrations to PostgreSQL and AlloyDB. The feature translates proprietary PL/SQL and T-SQL into PL/pgSQL directly in the Cloud console, cutting the months of manual dual-dialect rewriting that make procedural logic the last-mile bottleneck of a migration.

title: How to Pretty-Print Your Kubernetes YAML as KYAML and Why You'd Want To
blurb: Kubernetes SIG CLI introduced KYAML, a strict subset of standard YAML for writing manifests that parses with existing tooling and no new parser. It fixes the format's known traps by dropping whitespace-sensitive structure, always quoting strings to kill silent type coercion like the Norway Bug, and using explicit braces and brackets. The payoff is safer Helm templating and manifests that mean the same thing to every reader.

title: Lightweight Dragonfly Deployment: P2P Distribution Without the Database Stack
blurb: Dragonfly's peer-to-peer image distribution normally ships with a full control plane: a Manager backed by MySQL and Redis for dynamic config, multi-cluster coordination, and registry preheating. This post documents a lightweight deployment that drops all three, leaving the Scheduler as the sole coordinator and swapping the database stack for a ConfigMap and a headless Service. For a single cluster fighting registry overload on image pulls, it installs with one Helm command and cuts the operational surface to what a solo cluster actually needs.

title: A month with Anthropic’s Mythos left Rubrik rethinking remediation
blurb: Rubrik spent a month scanning its own code with Anthropic's Mythos Preview model and found so many issues it rebuilt its review pipeline instead of hiring reviewers. CTO Arvind Nithrakashyap argues the real engineering went into the harness wrapping the model and into deciding what not to automate: machine remediation covers only a well-scoped set of vulnerability classes, while everything else gets a structured plan and a human owner. The stated trade-off is trustworthy automation over maximum automation.

title: Node.js creator liberates Durable Objects from Cloudflare
blurb: Ryan Dahl, creator of Node.js and Deno, released celld, an open-source runtime that reimplements Cloudflare's Durable Objects so teams can run stateful, single-threaded actor workloads outside Cloudflare's platform. The project decouples the Durable Objects programming model from Workers and its proprietary storage layer, giving platform teams a self-hostable path that avoids vendor lock-in while keeping the same strong-consistency guarantees.

title: Brex watches AI agents at the network layer
blurb: Brex deployed the open-source OpenClaw agent against internal roles, then moved its security perimeter from the code to the network layer after its security team refused to trust an agent with unrestricted code execution. Rather than restricting tool usage the way Nvidia's NemoClaw does, Brex built CrabTrap to monitor what the agent's container actually sends and receives, preserving the coding capabilities while policing egress. CEO Pedro Franceschi argues the coding ability is the point, so the boundary belongs where the code talks to the outside world.

title: Deeply buried 16-year-old SQLite bug caused last year's Tailscale outages
blurb: A postmortem traces Tailscale's intermittent outages last year to a 16-year-old bug in SQLite's query planner, which under specific conditions returned incorrect results rather than erroring out. The root cause sat far beneath the application layer, in a dependency most teams treat as bulletproof, and evaded detection until the failure pattern was correlated across incidents. The takeaway for platform teams is that even battle-tested foundational libraries belong in the blast-radius analysis when debugging inexplicable data-layer behavior.

title: Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available
blurb: Cloudflare made Certificate Transparency Monitoring generally available, now filtering out its own routine certificate renewals so alerts only surface unexpected, mis-issued certs.

title: AWS wants to lower cloud compute crunch with Kubernetes updates
blurb: AWS added an advanced control-plane configuration to Amazon EKS, letting teams tune the Kubernetes API server, scheduler, and controller manager directly without running customized control-plane components. Four exposed parameters cover pod placement, HPA sync period, event retention, and NodePort ranges, aimed at high-churn batch, AI, and CI/CD workloads that previously required bespoke tuning and can now consolidate pods onto fewer nodes to cut compute cost.

title: LLMOps and platform engineering: Who should own the AI pipeline?
blurb: This CNCF post argues that LLMOps is a specialized layer on top of MLOps and DevOps, adding prompt versioning, GPU-backed inference serving, and output evaluation for tone and safety rather than clean accuracy scores. The author's core claim is that platform engineering should own the AI pipeline as another self-service golden path, or teams will recreate shadow IT with prompts instead of Jenkinsfiles. The practical guidance covers treating prompts as versioned artifacts and monitoring for model drift, cost creep, and degrading integrations after deployment.

title: DDoS attacks hit record scale as 1 Tbps+ campaigns become more common
blurb: Cloudflare's H1 2026 DDoS Threat Report found hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps became markedly more common, with April peaking at 6.46 trillion requests and 165 PB of traffic. Attackers increasingly blend network- and application-layer vectors mid-incident, though 96.62% of L3/4 attacks stayed under 500 Mbps and 90.6% ended within 10 minutes.

title: Testing ads in ChatGPT
blurb: OpenAI expanded its ChatGPT Ads pilot to the UK, Mexico, Brazil, Japan, and South Korea, after a US test that showed no drop in trust metrics and low ad-dismissal rates. Ads appear only for logged-in adults on the Free and Go tiers, don't influence answers, and keep conversations private from advertisers, giving marketers a new intent-rich placement inside the assistant itself.

title: How to make people care about your startup
blurb: Founder-led communication is now one of the lowest-cost, highest-leverage ways to earn attention as AI-generated content floods X and LinkedIn and buries generic startup posts. The piece maps three founder archetypes to distinct origin-story angles, arguing that the goal is not to be vulnerable or contrarian in every post but to say something honest and specific enough to cut through the noise. For founders who reach out saying "I have no idea what to say," the fix is turning your actual origin story into a repeatable comms strategy.

title: LinkedIn playbook offers guide to optimizing for AI
blurb: LinkedIn released a new playbook on optimizing content for AI citations, aimed at helping marketers boost credibility as more professionals query chatbots instead of running traditional searches. The guide covers tactics for earning citations in AI answers, from publishing authoritative posts to structuring content so tools like ChatGPT and Copilot surface it in responses.

title: AI search performance KPIs every marketer should track
blurb: Visitors arriving via AI search convert at 4.4x the rate of standard organic traffic, per Semrush, which means a brand can lose 40% of its traffic and still win in AI search while a #1-ranked competitor stays invisible across every AI engine. That gap is why traffic and rankings no longer tell the full story. HubSpot's guide lays out the AI search KPIs that do: visibility, citation share, AI-driven conversions, and revenue impact, plus how to tie each back to pipeline.

title: Perplexity cites ClickUp 6,474 times. Notion gets 741… Why?
blurb: Roughly half of every AI answer is unsolicited commentary the model adds on its own, and Profound's breakdown shows it clusters in the categories that decide purchases: rationale, comparison tables, rankings, and pricing caveats. Citations and search traffic come from different surfaces, so ranking in Google no longer guarantees you get cited. Notion pulls 5.46M monthly organic visits to ClickUp's 1.77M, yet Perplexity cites ClickUp 6,474 times to Notion's 741. Audit what AI engines say about you, not just whether you appear.

title: Meta Partnership Ads Outperform Licensed UGC Across $130M in Ad Spend, Report Finds
blurb: Meta Partnership Ads beat brand-run licensed UGC across $130M in spend, posting a 19% higher CTR, 10% higher conversion rate, and 5% lower CPA despite a 19% higher CPM, per Agentio's analysis of 65,000 ads from 137 brands. The gap widened in Search placements, where Partnership Ads hit a 143% higher CVR and 63% lower CPA. Winners fatigue after about 36 days, and holding tests to a $1,000 spend floor before killing them keeps misclassified winners alive.

title: 37 Proven Ways to Use AI in Marketing
blurb: Ahrefs compiled 37 AI marketing tactics from practitioners who documented their workflows, spanning SEO, content, and international marketing. The standout examples move past prompt tips to built tooling: an agent that reads Google's 168-page quality-rater handbook, then evaluates your page and a competitor's against it in minutes, and a keyword tool that pulls real volume, reads the SERP for intent, and counts page types in the top 10. The throughline is judgment plus automation, not automation alone.

title: Player Perceptions of Generative AI in Games: A Steam Review Analysis
blurb: A study of 508,192 Steam reviews found that games disclosing generative AI use receive lower recommendation rates and more negative sentiment than games using decades-old procedural content generation. Thematic coding of 600 reviews shows players read generative AI as a signal of low developer investment, not added value. The authors argue adoption succeeds only when generative AI solves a player need rather than cutting production costs, a useful frame for any PM weighing where to disclose AI in a shipped product.

title: DeadLock Ransomware Uses Polygon Smart Contracts to Make Extortion Infra Harder to Disrupt
blurb: DeadLock ransomware now runs its extortion infrastructure on Polygon smart contracts, storing and delivering victim-communication resources on-chain to resist takedowns, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The group, active since July 2025 and using Session messaging plus Bitcoin or Monero payments, has claimed 96 victims concentrated in Italy, Spain, Poland, Türkiye, and the US.

title: Coinbase Wins Abu Dhabi License for Tokenized Securities Hub
blurb: Coinbase received a Financial Services Permission from Abu Dhabi Global Market's regulator to build an international tokenization hub, clearing it to arrange deals and custody ahead of a tokenized securities launch. Tokens will be backed 1:1 by underlying shares under FSRA supervision, available only outside the US, with vested holders receiving voting and redemption rights and every transfer subject to sanctions screening.

title: Riot Signs $9.1B, 20-Year AI Data Center Lease at Its Texas Bitcoin Mine
blurb: Riot Platforms leased 191 megawatts at its Rockdale, Texas bitcoin mine to an unnamed frontier AI lab under a 20-year agreement Riot projects will generate roughly $9.1B, or about $457M a year. That is four times the $113.7M its mining business produced in Q2, when Riot posted a $237.2M net loss and a per-bitcoin cost exceeding production value once depreciation was included.

title: Kalshi in talks with Sequoia, Wellington for $750 million fund raise at $40 billion valuation
blurb: Kalshi is in advanced talks with Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management to raise at least $750M at a $40B valuation, nearly doubling the $22B mark it hit raising $1B in May. The round would give Wellington its first stake and deepen Sequoia's, as Kalshi hits roughly $4B in annualized revenue, claims 95% of the US prediction market, and eyes a 2027 IPO.

title: SEC clears Franklin Templeton funds to use onchain BENJI system for cash management
blurb: The SEC's Division of Investment Management issued Franklin Templeton a no-action letter allowing its traditional registered funds to hold shares of its blockchain-based OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund (BENJI) for cash management, exempting the arrangement from certain Rule 17f-2 physical-custody requirements. The decision lets conventional mutual funds and ETFs tap BENJI's onchain operational features, including faster settlement and more frequent pricing, without satisfying 1940 Act vault rules written for physical certificates.

title: MUFG to test real-time blockchain settlement for Japanese government bond trades
blurb: MUFG is preparing a proof-of-concept to settle Japanese government bond repo transactions onchain using the Canton network, targeting real-time 24/7 settlement versus the 1-3 days that JGB trades take today. The bank aims to improve capital and operational efficiency on repos, following JPMorgan's Kinexys network, which has run blockchain-based intraday US Treasury repos since 2020.

title: Standard Chartered Says Its $100 UNI Target May Be Too Low After Robinhood Chain Burns
blurb: Standard Chartered's Geoff Kendrick said his $100 end-2030 UNI price target may be too low, citing the pace at which Uniswap is now burning UNI with fees from its Robinhood Chain deployment. Uniswap's protocol revenue averaged $244,222 a day between Jul. 27 and Aug. 12, up 2.4x from the prior 17 days, with 60% of the burn coming from Robinhood Chain alone.

title: SEC Staff Clears Franklin Funds to Use Onchain Money Fund for Cash and Collateral
blurb: SEC staff granted Franklin Templeton no-action relief to let its registered funds hold shares of the tokenized Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund (FOBXX) as an internal cash and securities-lending collateral vehicle, subject to 12 conditions on segregation, controls, and independent verification. The relief waives vault-era Rule 17f-2 custody provisions for the blockchain-recorded BENJI shares, which held about $726.6M in assets as of Aug. 12.

title: Trezor shipping provider breach exposes personal data of nearly 14,000 customers
blurb: A breach at Trezor's shipping provider ShipMonk exposed the names, email addresses, phone numbers, and home addresses of roughly 13,700 hardware wallet customers across the US, UK, Sweden, Brazil, and other markets. Trezor said its internal systems and the wallets themselves remain secure, but affected users now face elevated risk of phishing and physical targeting, echoing prior Ledger breaches.

title: CFTC Sues Goliath Ventures Over Alleged $397M DeFi Liquidity Pool Ponzi
blurb: The CFTC sued Goliath Ventures and CEO Christopher Delgado, alleging the Florida firm raised at least $397M from roughly 1,600 customers to place their bitcoin and ether in DeFi liquidity pools but never deployed any funds, running a Ponzi scheme from November 2022 to February 2026. The complaint says Goliath misappropriated all customer money, paying $87M to earlier customers, $174M to insiders as recruiting commissions, and $48M to Delgado for homes, vehicles, and jewelry.

title: MoneyGram Brings Cash-To-Crypto Ramps To Solana
blurb: MoneyGram extended its Ramps cash-to-crypto API natively to Solana, letting wallets route users into its retail network without first bridging USDC to Stellar. The integration supports cash deposits in over 25 countries and withdrawals in more than 170, taps MoneyGram's ~500,000 retail locations, and debuts through self-custody trading app Rift on a chain holding $15.73B in stablecoins.

title: Ether.fi adds tokenized stocks, metals and Aave-powered portfolio loans in latest ‘neobank’ expansion
blurb: Ether.fi released "Summer," an upgrade to its non-custodial neobank app that adds tokenized stock and metal trading via xStocks, full-portfolio borrowing through Aave at rates near 4%, and expanded global fiat payments. The app holds assets in self-custodial vaults with social recovery and funds spending on the ether.fi Cash card, positioning the protocol as a bank replacement for its roughly 500,000 users and 150,000 cards.

title: Peter Thiel-backed Bullish posts $280 million Q2 net loss as digital asset sales fall 44%
blurb: Bullish posted a $280 million net loss in Q2, narrowing from $604.9 million in Q1 2026, as digital asset sales fell 44% to $32.6 billion. Adjusted revenue rose 62% year over year to $92.6 million, and record subscription and services revenue of $62.7 million offset weaker trading ahead of the exchange's proposed $4.2 billion Equiniti acquisition slated to close in early 2027.

title: Stablecoin Card Issuer Rain Buys Merchant Wallet Startup Ansa
blurb: Rain, a stablecoin card issuer, acquired merchant-wallet startup Ansa, whose white-label APIs let brands run prepaid closed-loop wallets like the Starbucks app. Rain plans to pair Ansa's stored balances with its own Visa and Mastercard issuing so prefunded funds can spend outside the issuing merchant, folding wallets, rewards, and stablecoins onto one platform. Ansa raised $19.4M total before the deal, and founder Sophia Goldberg becomes Rain's head of payments.

title: BitGo sees revenue jump 80% to $4.3 billion in Q2 but posts net loss
blurb: BitGo reported $4.33 billion in Q2 revenue, up 79.6% year-over-year, driven by higher digital asset sales and its stablecoin-as-a-service business, alongside 26% client growth and $65.2 billion in normalized platform assets. The custodian still posted a $19 million net loss, down from a $38.3 million profit a year earlier, after an $18.8 million unrealized loss on digital asset holdings.

title: eToro to Buy US Brokerage TradeZero for Up to $231M as Crypto Revenue Shrinks
blurb: eToro agreed to acquire US brokerage TradeZero for up to $231M in cash plus 2.5 million Class A shares, adding a registered US broker-dealer and its short-locator tools to expand equities trading. The deal lands as eToro's crypto revenue fell to $1.35B in Q2 from $1.91B a year earlier, with July crypto trades down 73% year-over-year.

title: Pump.fun's Share Of Launchpad Fees Fell To 27% In July. Four Weeks Later It's Back Above Half
blurb: Pump.fun's share of launchpad fees dropped to 26.7% in the week to July 14 as NOXA and other Robinhood Chain launchpads flooded in, then recovered to 51.7% by August 11, its largest weekly haul in 90 days. Category-wide fees nearly doubled to $75.39 million over the 30 days to August 11, so pump.fun's absolute weekly take hit a 90-day high even as competitors expanded the market.

title: Blockchain Association backs Custodia’s Supreme Court bid over Fed master account access
blurb: The Blockchain Association filed an amicus brief backing Custodia Bank's Supreme Court petition, which challenges whether regional Fed banks can deny master account access to eligible state-chartered institutions. Custodia, the Wyoming crypto bank founded by Caitlin Long, has lost at the district court, the 10th Circuit, and an en banc rehearing since first applying in 2020, making a master account the gating infrastructure for banks serving digital asset clients.

title: Robinhood Private-Market Fund Prices $200 Million IPO
blurb: Robinhood Ventures Fund II priced its IPO at $25 per share for 8 million shares, raising $200 million to give retail investors exchange-traded exposure to a portfolio of roughly 80 private companies. The business development company carries a 2% management fee plus a 20% incentive fee, uses leverage, and begins trading on the NYSE under the ticker RVII on Aug. 13.

title: Coinbase rolls out derivatives for UK professional investors
blurb: Coinbase launched regulated crypto derivatives for professional investors in the UK, offering perpetual futures under FCA oversight after the exchange secured the necessary permissions. The move extends Coinbase's derivatives footprint into a market where retail crypto derivatives remain banned, targeting institutional and professional traders who previously routed offshore for leveraged exposure.

title: Figure revenue doubles as blockchain loan marketplace volumes surge
blurb: Figure Technology Solutions reported $226 million in Q2 net revenue, up 113% year-over-year, as Consumer Loan Marketplace volume climbed 132% to $4.3 billion. Nearly two-thirds of that volume routed through Figure Connect, its blockchain marketplace linking loan originators with capital providers, and the company guided to $4.8 billion to $5.2 billion in marketplace volume for Q3.

title: Morgan Stanley's infrastructure partner Zerohash rebuffed in pitch to be U.S. trust bank
blurb: The OCC returned Zerohash's application for a U.S. national trust bank charter, ending the Chicago firm's initial bid over "material deficiencies" without a formal denial. Zerohash, which runs crypto backend operations for firms including Morgan Stanley's E*Trade, plans to re-file this month with a narrower scope, leaving it outside the wave of trust charters the regulator has recently granted to digital-asset firms.

title: South Korea sentences Delio CEO to 15 years in prison for $50 million crypto fraud: report
blurb: A Seoul court sentenced Delio CEO Jeong Sang-ho to 15 years in prison for embezzling roughly 70 billion won ($49.2M) in customer crypto assets and using false documents to register as a virtual asset service provider. The court acquitted Jeong on the larger 250 billion won ($175.6M) fraud charge over illegally collected evidence, falling short of the 20-year term prosecutors sought.

title: SharpLink Plans $200 Million ETH Allocation to Lido’s wstETH
blurb: SharpLink plans to stake $200 million of ETH through Lido, receiving roughly 106,000 wstETH held in custody with Anchorage Digital, or about 12% of the company's 888,938 ETH treasury. The move adds Lido's liquid-staking route alongside existing native ETH, Liquid Collective's LsETH, and Ether.fi's weETH positions, after a quarter in which staking supplied nearly all revenue but LsETH and weETH drew a $76.1 million impairment.

title: Barça Mobile Plans Stellar Wallet With Wirex and Crossmint
blurb: FC Barcelona's official mobile carrier, Barça Mobile, is building an in-app digital wallet on Stellar, using Crossmint for wallet infrastructure and onboarding and Wirex for payment and card rails. The feature extends the club's existing travel-eSIM app into payments, loyalty rewards, and travel services rather than launching as a standalone product, targeting the carrier's existing user base.

title: Mirae Asset to inject additional $35 million into Korbit crypto exchange following July acquisition: report
blurb: Mirae Asset will inject roughly 50 billion won ($35.3 million) into DigitalX, the operator of Korean crypto exchange Korbit, via a share issuance fully allotted to parent Mirae Asset Consulting. The capital follows Mirae Asset's July acquisition of 97.15% of the exchange for about 130 billion won ($91.5 million) and is earmarked for improving DigitalX's financial structure.

title: Securitize’s Tokenized Assets Hit $4.3 Billion as Revenue Falls
blurb: Securitize reported record tokenized assets under management of $4.3 billion in Q2, up 16% year over year, but revenue fell 5% to $14.4 million and its net loss widened to $21.7 million in its first results as a public company. Shares dropped about 16% in after-hours trading as tokenization revenue declined 12% even while transaction volume rose 147% year over year.

title: Uniswap Founder Says Team Renounced Creator Fees From Employee Testing
blurb: Uniswap founder Hayden Adams said the team renounced all creator fees from tokens generated during internal testing of Pools, redirecting past and future fees to a programmatic buyback-and-burn contract after the tokens were discovered. The redirected fees release as ETH claimable by burning the corresponding token, and Adams did not disclose how much had accrued or name the affected tokens.

title: BitGo CFO to Exit as Q2 Net Loss Hits $19 Million
blurb: BitGo CFO Edward Reginelli will resign effective Sept. 15, the same day the digital-asset custody firm reported a $19.0 million second-quarter net loss, reversing a $38.3 million profit a year earlier despite revenue climbing 79.6% to $4.33 billion. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $4.2 million loss as trading margins narrowed to 17 basis points, following a June cut of roughly 15% of staff targeting $15 million in annualized savings.

title: Swissquote cuts full-year guidance as 1H crypto income plunges, shares slide
blurb: Swissquote cut its full-year revenue and profit forecasts after first-half net crypto income fell 66.2% to 14.6 million Swiss francs ($18 million), with crypto trading volume down 63.5% to 2.58 billion francs. Shares in the Swiss bank fell 14% on the news, partly offset by a nearly 20% rise in client assets to 96.3 billion francs and gains in non-crypto trading and interest income.

title: Brazil’s largest bitcoin treasury firm plans ETF with 95% allocation to Strategy's STRC
blurb: OranjeBTC, Brazil's largest bitcoin treasury firm holding 3,950 BTC, plans to launch the DIGY11 ETF on the B3 exchange in early September, allocating 95% to Strategy's STRC preferred shares and 5% to Strive's SATA. The fund targets monthly distributions at Brazil's CDI rate plus 3-5 points, charges a 0.90% management fee, and hedges dollar exposure through monthly FX forwards.

title: US Senate advances CLARITY Act ahead of August recess
blurb: The US Senate advanced the CLARITY Act before breaking for August recess, moving the crypto market-structure bill past a key procedural hurdle after months of committee negotiation. The legislation splits oversight of digital assets between the SEC and CFTC, giving the CFTC primary jurisdiction over tokens deemed sufficiently decentralized and setting clearer registration rules for exchanges and issuers.

title: Boltz Founders Exit as Unnamed Bitcoin Group Agrees to Take Over Suspended Swap Service
blurb: Boltz's original founders stepped down effective immediately, handing its suspended Bitcoin swap service to an unnamed group of "veteran Bitcoiners" who will supply capital and engineering resources. The bootstrapped five-person startup halted swaps on Aug. 3 after AI-assisted attackers repeatedly breached the non-custodial service, causing losses without putting user funds at risk.

title: Bullish shares surge 14% as subscription revenue offsets digital asset slowdown
blurb: Bullish (BLSH) posted a $280 million Q2 net loss, driven mostly by a $244.6 million markdown on its bitcoin holdings as BTC fell 14% during the quarter. Record subscription and services revenue of $62.7 million offset a drop in digital asset sales to $32.6 billion from $58.6 billion, sending shares up nearly 14.5% to $28.20.

title: Strategy, Metaplanet unrealized bitcoin losses highlight risk of concentrating on just one token
blurb: Strategy and Metaplanet disclosed a combined $9.7 billion in unrealized bitcoin losses, with Strategy down $8.2 billion on its treasury and Tokyo-listed Metaplanet reporting a $1.5 billion paper loss on 43,000 BTC as of end-June. Both funded purchases largely with debt, concentrating balance-sheet risk in a single yieldless asset as BTC holds between $62,000 and $66,000.

title: Metaplanet denies selling bitcoin worth $320 million
blurb: Metaplanet CEO Simon Gerovich denied that the company sold any bitcoin, clarifying that a 5,014 BTC transfer worth $320 million flagged by on-chain trackers was a routine move between its own custodial addresses. The firm still holds 43,000 BTC, and the episode reflects heightened investor scrutiny of digital asset treasury companies for any sign that large corporate holders are trimming positions.

title: Securitize falls 20% after earnings miss as tokenization revenue falls short
blurb: Securitize shares fell 20% in after-hours trading Wednesday after the tokenization firm posted a $2.37 per-share loss against an expected $0.15 loss and revenue of $14.4 million, down 5% and short of the $20.6 million consensus. The miss came despite record tokenized assets under management of $4.3 billion and a 147% jump in transaction volume to $5.3 billion.

title: Circle’s cirBTC Is Live on Ethereum but Has Only 40 BTC Outstanding
blurb: Circle's cirBTC, an institutional bitcoin-collateral token backed 1:1 by BTC held through its OCC-supervised Circle National Trust custodian, has been live on Ethereum since June 8 but shows only ~40 tokens across 11 holder addresses. That trails WBTC's 116,000 and Coinbase's cbBTC's 97,000, and CoinGecko still labels the asset "preview only" with no listed exchange availability.

title: Prediction markets should dial back faulty filings for incentives to boost trading: CFTC
blurb: The CFTC issued guidance warning prediction-market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket that their filings for trading-incentive programs are increasingly deficient and may enable market abuse. The regulator flagged that high-volume rewards can drive wash-trading and pre-arranged trades, and that market-maker stipends and loss-covering rebates risk encouraging manipulation.

title: Bitcoin treasury company Metaplanet unveils BitBonds with $1.3 million private debt sale
blurb: Metaplanet, the Tokyo-listed bitcoin treasury company, launched a continuous bond issuance program called BitBonds, closing an inaugural round of four privately placed series worth about 200 million yen ($1.3 million) at 4% to 4.3% annual interest. The unsecured, unrated three-year notes give the firm a fixed-rate funding channel alongside equity, though repayment rests on a balance sheet still concentrated in its 43,000 BTC holdings.

title: Alabama residents left powerless to stop massive Bitcoin mining data center despite county and town moratoriums — hole in state zoning laws lets facility through
blurb: VoltCore is building a 50-MW Bitcoin mining data center in Somerville, Alabama, and neither the town nor Morgan County can stop it because a gap in state law leaves rural areas without any zoning authority. County moratoriums carry no legal weight since the site sits on private land, and residents have fallen back on petitions and a GoFundMe to hire a lawyer.

title: CFTC declares market emergency, orders Kalshi to continue to operate in New York
blurb: The CFTC invoked its emergency authority and ordered KalshiEX to keep operating in New York, overriding the state attorney general's bid to shut down its event-contract markets nationwide. The move escalates a jurisdictional fight over whether prediction markets are federally regulated derivatives or state-controlled gambling, with the CFTC now suing nine states to defend its exclusive authority over CFTC-registered exchanges.

title: Coinbase Wins Abu Dhabi License for Tokenized Securities Hub
blurb: Coinbase received a Financial Services Permission from Abu Dhabi Global Market's FSRA to build an international tokenization hub, clearing it to arrange and custody tokenized securities backed 1:1 by underlying shares for eligible investors outside the US. Holders will need only a wallet rather than a brokerage or correspondent-banking relationship, though voting and redemption rights are limited to vested holders and every transfer stays subject to sanctions screening with wallet-level freeze capability.

title: Riot Signs $9.1B, 20-Year AI Data Center Lease at Its Texas Bitcoin Mine
blurb: Riot Platforms leased 191 megawatts at its Rockdale, Texas bitcoin mining campus to an unnamed frontier AI lab under a 20-year agreement Riot values at roughly $9.1B, per an Aug. 10 SEC filing. The deal signals miners repricing cheap, grid-connected power for AI compute: Riot projects the lease to average $457M in annual revenue, four times its entire Q2 mining haul as that business ran at a net loss.

title: Kalshi in talks with Sequoia, Wellington for $750 million fund raise at $40 billion valuation
blurb: Kalshi is in advanced talks with Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management to raise at least $750 million at a $40 billion valuation, nearly doubling the $22 billion mark it hit in May. The round would deepen Sequoia's stake and mark Wellington's first bet on Kalshi, which now generates roughly $4 billion in annualized revenue, claims 95% of the US prediction market, and is eyeing a 2027 IPO.

title: SEC Staff Clears Franklin Funds to Use Onchain Money Fund for Cash and Collateral
blurb: SEC staff issued a no-action letter permitting Franklin Templeton's registered funds to hold shares of its onchain Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund (FOBXX) for cash management and securities-lending collateral, resolving a conflict with Rule 17f-2 custody provisions written for physical securities. The relief swaps vault-era procedures for digital controls across 12 conditions, giving FOBXX's $726.6M blockchain-recorded shares a path into mainstream fund operations with hourly NAV and intraday settlement.

title: MUFG to test real-time blockchain settlement for Japanese government bond trades
blurb: MUFG is preparing a proof-of-concept for onchain settlement of Japanese government bond repo transactions on the Canton network, aiming to compress the current 1-3 day cycle into real-time 24/7 settlement. The move follows JPMorgan's Kinexys network, which has run blockchain-based intraday US Treasury repos since 2020, and fits MUFG's broader push into tokenized finance alongside a planned SMBC-Mizuho stablecoin.

title: Ether.fi adds tokenized stocks, metals and Aave-powered portfolio loans in latest ‘neobank’ expansion
blurb: Ether.fi launched "Summer," an upgrade to its non-custodial neobank app that adds tokenized stock and metal trading via xStocks, full-portfolio borrowing against Aave at rates near 4%, and expanded global fiat payments. The wallet already anchors one of the largest crypto-native card programs, with roughly 500,000 users and 150,000 cards, and the update pushes it toward competing directly with centralized-exchange superapps and traditional banks.

title: Klarna and Zilch launch new paid membership packages
blurb: Klarna and Zilch both launched paid membership tiers to compete with credit card incumbents, with Klarna Max at €44.99 a month bundling 23 subscriptions and a metal card, priced below AmEx Platinum. Zilch, with over 5m customers, rolled out its first paid tiers at £2.99 and £3.99 a month, adding rewards and open-banking income verification as it repositions BNPL toward everyday spend.

title: MoneyGram Brings Cash-To-Crypto Ramps To Solana
blurb: MoneyGram extended MoneyGram Ramps, its cash-to-crypto on- and off-ramp API, natively to Solana, removing the prior requirement to bridge USDC to Stellar before routing users into its retail cash network. Going native on a chain holding $15.73B in stablecoins gives developers direct access to cash deposits in 25+ countries and withdrawals across 170+, backed by nearly 500,000 retail locations, with self-custody app Rift as the first integration.

title: India’s central bank wants AI to approve loans that humans would reject
blurb: The Reserve Bank of India proposed guidelines pushing lenders to deploy AI underwriting models that extend credit to thin-file borrowers whom traditional scorecards reject, part of a financial-inclusion push targeting India's large unbanked population. The move puts the RBI in the unusual position of encouraging looser algorithmic lending, raising questions about fair-lending oversight and default exposure as banks adopt models that override human rejection decisions.

title: Mapping the AI economy
blurb: Stripe published an analysis of its transaction data across thousands of AI companies, finding that the 100 largest by revenue reach 120 markets on average by their third year and draw 48% of revenue from outside their home markets. Beyond high-GDP hubs, India, Mexico, Poland, and the UAE showed outsized AI spend relative to overall Stripe volume, marking them as expansion targets where localized payment methods and pricing convert demand to revenue.

title: Report: Kalshi seeks $40B valuation, Sequoia and Wellington eye lead investor role
blurb: Kalshi is in talks to raise at a roughly $40B valuation, with Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management negotiating to co-lead the round, according to The Information. The figure nearly doubles the prediction market's $22B valuation from May 2026 and lands as annualized revenue tops $4B, cementing its CFTC-regulated model over crypto-native rival Polymarket, now raising at $20B.

title: SEC clears Franklin Templeton funds to use onchain BENJI system for cash management
blurb: The SEC's Division of Investment Management issued a no-action letter clearing Franklin Templeton's traditional registered funds to hold shares of its onchain BENJI money market fund for cash management, waiving certain Rule 17f-2 physical-vault custody requirements under the 1940 Act. The decision lets conventional mutual funds and ETFs tap the fund's faster settlement and more frequent pricing, signaling regulators now treat blockchain book-entry records as equivalent to legacy custody arrangements.

title: Amsterdam-based Adyen reports H1 2026 net revenue up 19% YoY to €1.3B, processed volumes up 24% YoY to €803.8B, and EBITDA of €641.5M; ADYEN.AS rises 12%+ (Adam Whittaker/Wall Street Journal)
blurb: Adyen reported H1 2026 net revenue up 19% YoY to €1.3B, with processed volumes climbing 24% to €803.8B and EBITDA reaching €641.5M at a 49% margin. Shares rose more than 12% on the results, as the Dutch payments processor's single-platform model keeps winning volume from enterprise merchants faster than costs grow.

title: Stablecoin Card Issuer Rain Buys Merchant Wallet Startup Ansa
blurb: Rain acquired Ansa, a startup whose white-label APIs and SDKs let merchants run their own branded prepaid wallets, with founder Sophia Goldberg joining as head of payments. Rain plans to pair Ansa's stored fiat balances with its Visa and Mastercard issuing so a prefunded balance can spend outside the merchant that loaded it, consolidating wallets, rewards, and stablecoins onto one platform.

title: BitGo sees revenue jump 80% to $4.3 billion in Q2 but posts net loss
blurb: BitGo reported $4.33B in Q2 revenue, up 79.6% year-over-year, driven by higher digital asset sales and growth in its stablecoin-as-a-service business, but posted a $19M net loss on an unrealized digital asset writedown. The custodian grew clients 26% and normalized platform assets 31% to $65.2B, though it cut staff 15% in June and authorized a $50M share buyback.

title: eToro to Buy US Brokerage TradeZero for Up to $231M as Crypto Revenue Shrinks
blurb: eToro agreed to acquire US brokerage TradeZero for up to $231M in cash plus 2.5 million Class A shares, adding a regulated US broker-dealer and short-locator tooling as its crypto revenue contracts. Cryptoasset revenue fell to $1.35B in Q2 from $1.91B a year earlier, pushing eToro toward equities, where net trading income rose to $141.6M and funded accounts grew 18% to 4.28 million.

title: Blockchain Association backs Custodia’s Supreme Court bid over Fed master account access
blurb: The Blockchain Association filed an amicus brief supporting Custodia Bank's Supreme Court petition, which challenges the Kansas City Fed's denial of a master account and asks whether regional Fed banks can reject eligible state-chartered institutions. A master account grants direct access to Fed payment rails, so the ruling would determine whether crypto-focused banks can settle without leaning on sponsor-bank intermediaries.

title: Robinhood Private-Market Fund Prices $200 Million IPO
blurb: Robinhood Ventures Fund II priced its IPO at $25 per share to raise $200M gross, opening its 80-company private-startup portfolio to retail investors with no accreditation requirement or investment minimum. The vehicle is a business development company charging a 2% management fee plus 20% of realized gains, and its shares can trade above or below net asset value with no redemption right.

title: Deutsche Bank becomes first foreign yuan clearing bank in Europe
blurb: The People's Bank of China authorized Deutsche Bank to clear renminbi transactions from Frankfurt, making it the first foreign institution in Europe to hold the designation, a role until now reserved for Chinese lenders like Bank of China and ICBC. The move extends Beijing's overseas yuan-clearing network to a major European bank and gives manufacturers and automakers with Chinese suppliers a direct settlement route that avoids routing payments through the dollar.

title: Coinbase rolls out derivatives for UK professional investors
blurb: Coinbase launched regulated crypto derivatives for UK professional investors, extending the CFTC-regulated perpetual-style futures product it already offers in the US and EU to a new market under FCA oversight. The move lets Coinbase capture UK institutional trading volume that had migrated offshore to venues like Binance and Bybit, while operating inside a regulated perimeter that most crypto-native exchanges cannot match.

title: Barça Mobile Plans Stellar Wallet With Wirex and Crossmint
blurb: Barça Mobile, FC Barcelona's official MVNO operated by New Era Visionary Group, is building an in-app digital wallet using infrastructure from Wirex, Crossmint, and the Stellar Development Foundation, with Stellar as the blockchain layer and Wirex handling payment and card rails. The move extends the club's travel-eSIM app into payments, loyalty, and rewards, embedding wallet functionality into an existing consumer telecom product rather than launching a standalone fintech.

title: Figure revenue doubles as blockchain loan marketplace volumes surge
blurb: Figure Technology Solutions posted $226M in second-quarter net revenue, up 113% year-over-year, as Consumer Loan Marketplace volume jumped 132% to $4.3B, roughly two-thirds of it routed through its Figure Connect origination marketplace. The blockchain lender expects $4.8B to $5.2B in third-quarter marketplace volume and remains on track to close its Kiavi acquisition in the second half of 2026, pushing further into real estate lending.

title: Why JPMorgan is investing big in the 2028 LA Olympics
blurb: JPMorgan signed on as the Olympics' first global banking partner, a nine-figure deal covering the 2028 LA Games and 2030 French Alps Games at a reported $200M-plus per cycle. The bank paired the sponsorship with a 30% increase in Southern California business bankers, targeting its 5M consumer and 589,000 small-business clients in LA to convert brand spend into account acquisition.

title: Morgan Stanley's infrastructure partner Zerohash rebuffed in pitch to be U.S. trust bank
blurb: The OCC returned Zerohash's application for a digital-asset trust bank charter, ending the bid over "material deficiencies" while stopping short of a formal denial, unlike the outright rejections handed to two other fintechs. Zerohash, which runs crypto plumbing for Morgan Stanley's E*Trade, plans to re-file by month's end with a narrower scope, leaving it the lone holdout among the wave of firms the OCC has recently granted provisional trust charters.

title: Analysis: Why Revolut Survived and the Metaverse Didn't, a Tale of Financial Fashions
blurb: Lex argues that financial "metas" like ICOs, NFTs, and AI agents can pull in billions before any real economy shows up, and offers five tests to tell a passing fashion from durable infrastructure: external revenue, miracle count, chokepoints, boring prices, and clock speed. The case study is Virtuals, which peaked at $16.5M in monthly fees before collapsing more than 90% in four months even as the tech kept working. The distinction that matters is whether value rests on continued attention or survives on real customers, cash flows, and distribution.

title: HSBC Asset Management invests in London-founded Model ML
blurb: HSBC Asset Management took an equity stake in Model ML, the London-founded AI automation startup for financial services, pushing its total raised past $100M after a $75M Series A last November. The vertical-AI vendor, which counts Deloitte and PwC as clients and routes each task to the best-suited model, will use the funding to win banking and asset-manager accounts.

title: HSBC Asset Management backs AI finance group Model ML
blurb: HSBC Asset Management invested in Model ML, a 2023-founded startup building a model-agnostic orchestration engine that automates financial research, due diligence, and document generation while enforcing enterprise governance and auditability. The deal, made through HSBC's flagship VC strategy within its $81B alternatives platform on undisclosed terms, signals institutional conviction that vertical AI software, not any single model, is the differentiator for automating financial-services workflows.

title: Securitize’s Tokenized Assets Hit $4.3 Billion as Revenue Falls
blurb: Securitize reported record average tokenized assets under management of $4.3B in Q2, up 16% year over year, but revenue fell 5% to $14.4M and its net loss widened to $21.7M in its first results as a public company. Tokenization revenue dropped 12% even as transaction volume rose 147%, and shares fell about 16% in after-hours trading, giving investors an early read on whether tokenized-fund growth converts to revenue.

title: Danish Entravel Group raises €6.5 million to secure larger supplier credit facilities
blurb: Entravel Group raised €6.5M, co-led by Ethereal Ventures and Finality Capital, to expand supplier credit facilities and stablecoin settlement.

title: Swissquote cuts full-year guidance as 1H crypto income plunges, shares slide
blurb: Swissquote cut its full-year revenue and profit forecasts after first-half net crypto income fell 66.2% to 14.6 million francs ($18 million), with crypto trading volume down 63.5% and a 5.3 million-franc loss on the inventory backing its SQX exchange. Growth in non-crypto trading and interest income kept revenue broadly level and client assets up nearly 20% to 96.3 billion francs, but shares still fell 14% on the revised guidance.

title: Prediction markets should dial back faulty filings for incentives to boost trading: CFTC
blurb: The CFTC issued guidance warning prediction-market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket that their incentive and market-maker programs are increasingly built on deficient filings that could enable wash-trading and manipulation. The regulator flagged volume-based rewards and guaranteed market-maker stipends as compliance risks, tightening scrutiny of an event-contracts industry it proposed its first formal rule for in June.

title: Accelerant, which uses data analytics to connect insurance underwriters with risk capital partners, agrees to go private with Thoma Bravo in a $4.4B deal (Katherine Hamilton/Wall Street Journal)
blurb: Accelerant agreed to go private with Thoma Bravo in a $4.4B deal, taking the insurance-risk-exchange platform off the public markets roughly a year after its IPO. The company uses data analytics to match underwriters with risk-capital partners, and the buyout adds to Thoma Bravo's growing bet on insurance-infrastructure software as private equity deepens its position in the sector.

title: Securitize falls 20% after earnings miss as tokenization revenue falls short
blurb: Securitize shares fell 20% in after-hours trading Wednesday after the tokenization firm posted a $2.37 per-share loss, far wider than the $0.15 loss analysts expected, with revenue down 5% to $14.4 million. The miss lands even as tokenized assets under management hit a record $4.3 billion and transaction volume jumped 147%, showing on-chain activity still outpaces the revenue it generates.
